docs.title: ScrollSwarm
docs.text:
A 2D multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) testbed for cooperative UAV swarm reconnaissance, obstacle avoidance, and graph communication.

ScrollSwarm is a lightweight, high-throughput multi-agent simulation where autonomous drones fly forward through an aerial corridor, dodging obstacles while coordinating to photograph targets along their path:

  • Corridor & Altitude Control: Drones cruise forward at a constant speed (\(v_{\text{scroll}} = 1\text{ px/step}\)) and choose one discrete vertical action per step: climb up, dive down, or stay level.
  • Procedural Obstacles: 2D obstacles of varying shapes and sizes populate the corridor, while a minimum navigable gap (\(G_{\min} \ge 110\text{ px}\)) guarantees paths are never blocked.
  • Probabilistic Target Photography: Drones inspect targets within range (\(D_{\text{photo}} = 45\text{ px}\)), where photo success increases with proximity. Spreading across altitudes provides redundancy (\(P_{\text{team}} = 1 - \prod (1 - P_j)\)) so at least one drone captures each target.
  • Forward LiDAR & Bearings: Each drone scans forward with 7 LiDAR rays to detect oncoming obstacles and tracks relative bearings to the nearest target and teammate.
  • Graph Communication: Living drones exchange messages over configurable network graphs (chain, ring, full, radius, or capped) with native PyTorch Geometric (PyG) tensor export.
  • Crash Handling: Hitting any obstacle or corridor boundary causes that drone to crash immediately, while surviving teammates continue the mission.

docs.title: Key Highlights
docs.text: Feature Description PettingZoo Standard Natively implements Farama's ParallelEnv for seamless integration with modern MARL libraries. CTDE Ready Exposes centralized state vectors (\(\mathbb{R}^{16N}\)) for centralized training with decentralized execution (MAPPO, QMIX, MADDPG). Graph Neural Networks Exports PyTorch Geometric compatible edge_index \((2, E)\) and edge_attr \((E, 3)\) tensors for relational GNN learning. High Throughput Multi-backend compute engine (NumPy, Numba LLVM JIT, native C++20) delivering up to \(50\times\) isolated raycasting speedup and 1,700+ environment steps/sec per CPU core. Zero Bloat & Pluggable Pure NumPy baseline by default, with optional C++20 and Numba acceleration selectable via backend="auto".

docs.title: Agent & Dynamics API
docs.text: The agent module defines the physical autonomous quadcopter UAV entity, movement kinematics, discrete actions, and agent group generation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Entity Model: 2D quadcopter with fixed longitudinal station-keeping column, dynamic vertical position \(y(t)\), and bounding hitbox (\(20 \times 16\text{ px}\)).
  • Kinematic Update: \(\Delta y = -k\) (UP), \(\Delta y = 0\) (STAY), \(\Delta y = +k\) (DOWN), clamped to corridor boundary margins.
  • Collision & Lifecycle: Immediate crash (alive = False) upon boundary or obstacle contact.

docs.text:
from scrollswarm.agent import Agent, Action, create_agents

# Create a coordinated swarm of 5 quadcopters
agents = create_agents(num_agents=5, map_width=800, map_height=400)

for agent in agents:
    # Execute climb action
    agent.step(Action.UP, map_height=400)
    print(f"UAV {agent.agent_id} at ({agent.x}, {agent.y}), Alive: {agent.alive}")

class Agent:
    """
    Autonomous survey UAV (quadcopter) entity in ScrollSwarm.

    Each agent occupies a fixed horizontal column and navigates vertically
    (UP / STAY / DOWN) with a configurable step size.  The agent is represented
    as a forward-facing triangle for collision geometry and rendered as a
    quadcopter sprite in ``render_mode="human"``.

    Attributes:
        agent_id: Zero-based integer index of this drone in the swarm.
        x: Fixed horizontal position in pixels (column station-keeping).
        y: Current vertical position in pixels (mutable each step).
        step_size: Vertical displacement per UP/DOWN action in pixels.
        width: Horizontal collision bounding box extent in pixels.
        height: Vertical collision bounding box extent in pixels.
        color: RGB tuple used for rendering this drone.
        alive: ``False`` after any boundary or obstacle collision.
        score: Cumulative count of targets successfully photographed.
        steps_alive: Number of steps the drone has survived.
        collision_radius: Effective radius for obstacle proximity checks.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        agent_id: int,
        x: float,
        y: float,
        step_size: int = 5,
        width: float = 20.0,
        height: float = 16.0,
        color: Optional[Tuple[int, int, int]] = None,
        safe_proximity_dist: float = 28.0,
        backend: str = "auto",
    ):
        """
        Initializes the UAV agent.

        Args:
            agent_id: Zero-based drone index; also selects the color palette
                entry and is used to build the PettingZoo agent ID string.
            x: Initial horizontal position in pixels (fixed for the episode).
            y: Initial vertical position in pixels (dynamic).
            step_size: Vertical displacement per UP / DOWN action in pixels.
                Valid range: [1, 20].
            width: Physical horizontal bounding extent of the quadcopter body
                in pixels (used for collision triangle geometry).
            height: Physical vertical bounding extent in pixels.
            color: RGB tuple override.  Defaults to the palette entry for
                ``agent_id``.
            safe_proximity_dist: Minimum safe separation distance from other
                drones in pixels (retained for legacy proximity checks).
            backend: Acceleration backend for geometric raycasting. Options:
                ``"auto"``, ``"numpy"``, ``"numba"``, or ``"cpp"``.
        """
        self.agent_id = agent_id
        self.x = float(x)
        self.y = float(y)
        self.step_size = step_size
        self.width = float(width)
        self.height = float(height)
        self.color = (
            color if color is not None else AGENT_PALETTE[agent_id % len(AGENT_PALETTE)]
        )
        self.safe_proximity_dist = float(safe_proximity_dist)
        self.backend = backend

        # Operational state
        self.alive: bool = True
        self.score: int = 0
        self.steps_alive: int = 0

        # Collision radius for physical obstacle/boundary contact
        self.collision_radius: float = max(self.width, self.height) / 2.0

        # Perception sensor
        self.sensor: Optional[RaySensor] = None

    @property
    def vertices(self) -> List[Tuple[float, float]]:
        """
        Calculates the 3 vertices of the quadcopter facing forward (RIGHT):

        - Tip: (x + width / 2, y)
        - Top-Left: (x - width / 2, y - height / 2)
        - Bottom-Left: (x - width / 2, y + height / 2)
        """
        half_w = self.width / 2.0
        half_h = self.height / 2.0
        tip = (self.x + half_w, self.y)
        top_left = (self.x - half_w, self.y - half_h)
        bot_left = (self.x - half_w, self.y + half_h)
        return [tip, top_left, bot_left]

    def step(self, action: int, map_height: int) -> None:
        """
        Executes vertical movement:
        - UP: y decreases by step_size (k = 5 px)
        - DOWN: y increases by step_size (k = 5 px)
        - STAY: y remains unchanged
        """
        if not self.alive:
            return

        self.steps_alive += 1

        if action == Action.UP:
            self.y -= self.step_size
        elif action == Action.DOWN:
            self.y += self.step_size

        # Clamp within screen bounds
        half_h = self.height / 2.0
        self.y = float(np.clip(self.y, half_h, map_height - half_h))

    def check_collision_boundary(self, scrolling_map: ScrollingMap) -> bool:
        """
        Checks if any vertex of the UAV penetrates the upper ceiling or ground boundaries.
        Instant termination occurs on collision.
        """
        if not self.alive:
            return False

        for vx, vy in self.vertices:
            col = int(np.clip(np.round(vx), 0, scrolling_map.width - 1))
            top_bound = scrolling_map.top_heights[col]
            bot_bound = scrolling_map.height - scrolling_map.bot_heights[col]

            if vy <= top_bound or vy >= bot_bound:
                self.alive = False
                return True

        return False

    def check_collision_mountain(self, scrolling_map: ScrollingMap) -> bool:
        """Backward compatibility alias for check_collision_boundary."""
        return self.check_collision_boundary(scrolling_map)

    def check_collision_obstacles(self, obstacles: List[Any]) -> bool:
        """
        Checks physical collision with obstacles (buildings, overhead towers, floating debris).
        Instant termination occurs on contact.
        """
        if not self.alive:
            return False

        for obs in obstacles:
            if hasattr(obs, "distance_to_point"):
                dist = obs.distance_to_point(self.x, self.y)
                if dist <= self.collision_radius or obs.contains_point(self.x, self.y):
                    self.alive = False
                    return True
            elif hasattr(obs, "outer_radius"):
                dx = self.x - obs.x
                dy = self.y - obs.y
                threshold = self.collision_radius + obs.outer_radius
                if dx * dx + dy * dy <= threshold * threshold:
                    self.alive = False
                    return True

        return False

    def check_collision_trees(self, trees: List[Any]) -> bool:
        """Backward compatibility alias for check_collision_obstacles."""
        return self.check_collision_obstacles(trees)

    def compute_proximity_penalty(
        self,
        other_agents: List["Agent"],
        safe_dist: Optional[float] = None,
        penalty_coef: float = 0.5,
    ) -> float:
        """Backward compatibility stub (proximity penalty disabled in this scenario)."""
        return 0.0

    def check_target_inspection(
        self,
        targets: List[Target],
        rng: Optional[np.random.Generator] = None,
        team_drones: Optional[List["Agent"]] = None,
    ) -> int:
        """
        Inspects targets within photo radius using stochastic action uncertainty.
        Increments score and marks target collected upon successful photo.
        Returns number of targets successfully photographed.
        """
        if not self.alive:
            return 0

        generator = rng if rng is not None else np.random.default_rng()
        drones_pool = team_drones if team_drones is not None else [self]

        collected_count = 0
        for target in targets:
            if target.collected:
                continue

            dx = self.x - target.x
            dy = self.y - target.y
            dist = np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)

            # Check if this UAV is within inspection range
            if dist <= target.inspection_radius:
                success = target.sample_inspection(drones_pool, generator)
                if success:
                    self.score += 1
                    collected_count += 1

        return collected_count

    def check_target_collection(self, targets: List[Target]) -> int:
        """Backward compatibility alias for deterministic / direct target pickup."""
        if not self.alive:
            return 0

        collected_count = 0
        for target in targets:
            if target.collected:
                continue
            dx = self.x - target.x
            dy = self.y - target.y
            dist_sq = dx * dx + dy * dy
            threshold = self.collision_radius + target.size
            if dist_sq <= threshold * threshold:
                target.collected = True
                self.score += 1
                collected_count += 1

        return collected_count

    def reset(self, initial_y: float) -> None:
        """Resets the UAV to an initial vertical position and alive state."""
        self.y = float(initial_y)
        self.alive = True
        self.score = 0
        self.steps_alive = 0

    def get_observation(
        self,
        scrolling_map: ScrollingMap,
        other_agents: Optional[List["Agent"]] = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Computes the 16-dimensional continuous observation vector:
        [self_y / H, 7 obstacle ray distances, 4 target features, 4 neighbor features].
        """
        if self.sensor is None:
            self.sensor = RaySensor(
                max_range=float(scrolling_map.width) / 2.0,
                safe_proximity_dist=self.safe_proximity_dist,
                backend=self.backend,
            )
        return self.sensor.observe(
            origin_x=self.x,
            origin_y=self.y,
            scrolling_map=scrolling_map,
            other_agents=other_agents,
            agent_id=self.agent_id,
        )

def step(self, action: int, map_height: int) -> None:
    """
    Executes vertical movement:
    - UP: y decreases by step_size (k = 5 px)
    - DOWN: y increases by step_size (k = 5 px)
    - STAY: y remains unchanged
    """
    if not self.alive:
        return

    self.steps_alive += 1

    if action == Action.UP:
        self.y -= self.step_size
    elif action == Action.DOWN:
        self.y += self.step_size

    # Clamp within screen bounds
    half_h = self.height / 2.0
    self.y = float(np.clip(self.y, half_h, map_height - half_h))

def create_agents(
    num_agents: int = 5,
    map_width: int = 800,
    scrolling_map: Optional[ScrollingMap] = None,
    step_size: int = 5,
    backend: str = "auto",
) -> List[Agent]:
    """
    Creates a team of N UAVs (1 <= N <= 10, default 5).
    UAVs occupy fixed, evenly spaced horizontal columns on the left portion of the corridor.
    """
    if not (1 <= num_agents <= 10):
        raise ValueError(f"num_agents must be between 1 and 10, got {num_agents}")

    agents: List[Agent] = []
    x_min = 80.0
    x_max = min(320.0, float(map_width) * 0.45)

    for i in range(num_agents):
        if num_agents == 1:
            x_pos = (x_min + x_max) / 2.0
        else:
            x_pos = x_min + i * (x_max - x_min) / (num_agents - 1)

        # Center agent vertically in corridor
        if scrolling_map is not None:
            col = int(np.clip(np.round(x_pos), 0, scrolling_map.width - 1))
            top_bound = scrolling_map.top_heights[col]
            bot_bound = scrolling_map.height - scrolling_map.bot_heights[col]
            initial_y = (top_bound + bot_bound) / 2.0
        else:
            initial_y = 200.0

        color = AGENT_PALETTE[i % len(AGENT_PALETTE)]
        agents.append(
            Agent(
                agent_id=i,
                x=x_pos,
                y=initial_y,
                step_size=step_size,
                color=color,
                backend=backend,
            )
        )

    return agents

class CommunicationGraph:
    """
    Manages communication topology, dynamic edge pruning, and message passing
    across the ScrollSwarm multi-agent swarm.

    The graph is recomputed dynamically each step based on agent liveness and,
    for spatial topologies (``RADIUS``, ``CAPPED``), agent positions.  Dead
    agents (``alive == False``) are immediately pruned: their rows and columns
    in the adjacency matrix are zeroed.

    Attributes:
        topology: Active ``TopologyType`` governing edge construction.
        radius: Maximum communication range in pixels (used by ``RADIUS``).
        max_degree: Maximum number of neighbors per drone (used by ``CAPPED``).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        topology: Union[TopologyType, str] = TopologyType.CHAIN,
        radius: float = 180.0,
        max_degree: int = 2,
    ):
        """
        Initializes the CommunicationGraph.

        Args:
            topology: Graph topology to use.  Pass a ``TopologyType`` enum
                value or its string equivalent (e.g. ``"chain"``).
            radius: Communication radius in pixels for the ``RADIUS`` topology.
                Drones further apart than this do not share edges.
            max_degree: Maximum number of incoming neighbors per drone for the
                ``CAPPED`` topology.
        """
        if isinstance(topology, str):
            topology = TopologyType(topology.lower())
        self.topology = topology
        self.radius = float(radius)
        self.max_degree = max_degree

    def get_adjacency_matrix(self, agents: List[Agent]) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Computes the binary adjacency matrix for the current swarm state.

        ``A[i, j] = 1`` if a directed edge exists from agent ``j`` to agent
        ``i`` (i.e., agent ``i`` receives a message from agent ``j``).
        Dead agents (``alive == False``) have strictly zero rows and columns.

        Args:
            agents: Ordered list of all ``Agent`` instances in the swarm.

        Returns:
            Binary ``np.ndarray`` of shape ``(N, N)`` and dtype ``float32``.
        """
        n = len(agents)
        if n == 0:
            return np.zeros((0, 0), dtype=np.float32)

        adj = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=np.float32)
        alive_mask = np.array([a.alive for a in agents], dtype=bool)

        # Positions: (N, 2)
        positions = np.array([[a.x, a.y] for a in agents], dtype=np.float32)

        if self.topology == TopologyType.CHAIN:
            # Agent i connects to adjacent column neighbors i-1 and i+1
            for i in range(n):
                if i > 0:
                    adj[i, i - 1] = 1.0
                if i < n - 1:
                    adj[i, i + 1] = 1.0

        elif self.topology == TopologyType.RING:
            for i in range(n):
                if n > 1:
                    adj[i, (i - 1) % n] = 1.0
                    adj[i, (i + 1) % n] = 1.0

        elif self.topology == TopologyType.FULL:
            # Complete graph (all-to-all, zero on diagonal)
            adj = np.ones((n, n), dtype=np.float32)
            np.fill_diagonal(adj, 0.0)

        elif self.topology == TopologyType.RADIUS:
            # Spatial distance graph
            diff = positions[:, np.newaxis, :] - positions[np.newaxis, :, :]
            dist = np.sqrt(np.sum(diff**2, axis=-1))
            adj = (dist <= self.radius) & (dist > 1e-4)
            adj = adj.astype(np.float32)

        elif self.topology == TopologyType.CAPPED:
            # k-nearest spatial neighbors (max_degree)
            diff = positions[:, np.newaxis, :] - positions[np.newaxis, :, :]
            dist = np.sqrt(np.sum(diff**2, axis=-1))
            np.fill_diagonal(dist, np.inf)

            k = min(self.max_degree, max(0, n - 1))
            if k > 0:
                for i in range(n):
                    nearest_indices = np.argsort(dist[i])[:k]
                    for j in nearest_indices:
                        if not np.isinf(dist[i, j]):
                            adj[i, j] = 1.0

        # Enforce dead agent pruning: no edges to or from dead agents
        adj = adj * alive_mask[:, np.newaxis] * alive_mask[np.newaxis, :]
        return adj

    def get_edge_index_and_attributes(
        self,
        agents: List[Agent],
        map_width: float = 800.0,
        map_height: float = 400.0,
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Extracts active edges in PyTorch Geometric (PyG) COO format.

        Args:
            agents: Ordered list of all ``Agent`` instances in the swarm.
            map_width: Corridor width in pixels, used to normalize ``dx``.
            map_height: Corridor height in pixels, used to normalize ``dy``.

        Returns:
            edge_index: Integer array of shape ``(2, E)`` where
                ``edge_index[0]`` contains source node indices (``j``) and
                ``edge_index[1]`` contains target node indices (``i``).
            edge_attr: Float32 array of shape ``(E, 3)`` with normalized
                relative spatial features ``[dx/W, dy/H, dist/diag]`` for
                each directed edge ``j → i``.
        """
        adj = self.get_adjacency_matrix(agents)
        target_indices, source_indices = np.where(adj > 0.5)

        # PyG convention: [source, target] = [j, i]
        edge_index = np.stack([source_indices, target_indices], axis=0).astype(np.int64)
        num_edges = edge_index.shape[1]

        if num_edges == 0:
            return edge_index, np.zeros((0, 3), dtype=np.float32)

        positions = np.array([[a.x, a.y] for a in agents], dtype=np.float32)
        diag = np.sqrt(map_width**2 + map_height**2)

        src_pos = positions[source_indices]
        tgt_pos = positions[target_indices]

        dx = (src_pos[:, 0] - tgt_pos[:, 0]) / map_width
        dy = (src_pos[:, 1] - tgt_pos[:, 1]) / map_height
        dist = (
            np.sqrt(
                (src_pos[:, 0] - tgt_pos[:, 0]) ** 2
                + (src_pos[:, 1] - tgt_pos[:, 1]) ** 2
            )
            / diag
        )

        edge_attr = np.stack([dx, dy, dist], axis=-1).astype(np.float32)
        return edge_index, edge_attr

    def route_messages(
        self,
        messages: Dict[Union[int, str], np.ndarray],
        agents: List[Agent],
        aggregation: str = "mean",
        message_dim: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Routes and aggregates neighbor messages across the communication graph.

        Each living agent ``i`` collects the messages of its in-neighbors
        ``j ∈ N(i)`` and aggregates them according to the chosen operator.
        Isolated or dead agents receive a zero vector.

        Args:
            messages: Dict mapping agent ID (``int`` or ``"agent_i"`` string)
                to a 1-D message array of shape ``(M,)``.
            agents: Ordered list of all ``Agent`` instances in the swarm.
            aggregation: Aggregation function applied across in-neighbor
                messages.  One of:

                - ``"mean"`` *(default)* — permutation-invariant mean pooling.
                - ``"sum"`` — cumulative sum (sensitive to degree).
                - ``"max"`` — element-wise maximum (saliency filtering).
                - ``"concat"`` — concatenation up to ``max_degree`` neighbors
                  (fixed-size; order is arbitrary).

            message_dim: Dimensionality ``M`` of each message.  Inferred
                from the first entry of ``messages`` if omitted.

        Returns:
            Dict mapping ``"agent_i"`` to the aggregated neighbor message
            array of shape ``(M,)`` (or ``(M * k,)`` for ``"concat"``).

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``aggregation`` is not one of the four supported
                operators.
        """
        adj = self.get_adjacency_matrix(agents)
        n = len(agents)

        # Infer message dimension M
        if message_dim is None:
            for val in messages.values():
                message_dim = val.shape[0]
                break
            if message_dim is None:
                message_dim = 1

        # Standardize message lookup
        msg_tensor = np.zeros((n, message_dim), dtype=np.float32)
        for i, a in enumerate(agents):
            if not a.alive:
                continue
            key_int = a.agent_id
            key_str = f"agent_{a.agent_id}"
            if key_int in messages:
                msg_tensor[i] = messages[key_int]
            elif key_str in messages:
                msg_tensor[i] = messages[key_str]

        inbox: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

        for i, agent in enumerate(agents):
            agent_key = f"agent_{agent.agent_id}"
            if not agent.alive:
                inbox[agent_key] = np.zeros(message_dim, dtype=np.float32)
                continue

            # In-neighbors of agent i: indices j where adj[i, j] > 0
            neighbor_indices = np.where(adj[i] > 0.5)[0]

            if len(neighbor_indices) == 0:
                # Isolated node or no alive neighbors
                inbox[agent_key] = np.zeros(message_dim, dtype=np.float32)
            else:
                neighbor_msgs = msg_tensor[neighbor_indices]  # (K, M)

                if aggregation == "mean":
                    inbox[agent_key] = np.mean(neighbor_msgs, axis=0)
                elif aggregation == "sum":
                    inbox[agent_key] = np.sum(neighbor_msgs, axis=0)
                elif aggregation == "max":
                    inbox[agent_key] = np.max(neighbor_msgs, axis=0)
                elif aggregation == "concat":
                    # Flatten up to max_degree neighbors
                    inbox[agent_key] = neighbor_msgs.flatten()
                else:
                    raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation: {aggregation}")

        return inbox

    def get_communication_edges(
        self,
        agents: List[Agent],
    ) -> List[Tuple[Tuple[float, float], Tuple[float, float]]]:
        """
        Returns line segment coordinates [(p_source, p_target)] for active edges,
        convenient for visual rendering in Pygame or debugging.
        """
        adj = self.get_adjacency_matrix(agents)
        n = len(agents)
        edges = []
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                # If connected in either direction
                if adj[i, j] > 0.5 or adj[j, i] > 0.5:
                    edges.append(
                        ((agents[i].x, agents[i].y), (agents[j].x, agents[j].y))
                    )
        return edges

def route_messages(
    self,
    messages: Dict[Union[int, str], np.ndarray],
    agents: List[Agent],
    aggregation: str = "mean",
    message_dim: Optional[int] = None,
) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Routes and aggregates neighbor messages across the communication graph.

    Each living agent ``i`` collects the messages of its in-neighbors
    ``j ∈ N(i)`` and aggregates them according to the chosen operator.
    Isolated or dead agents receive a zero vector.

    Args:
        messages: Dict mapping agent ID (``int`` or ``"agent_i"`` string)
            to a 1-D message array of shape ``(M,)``.
        agents: Ordered list of all ``Agent`` instances in the swarm.
        aggregation: Aggregation function applied across in-neighbor
            messages.  One of:

            - ``"mean"`` *(default)* — permutation-invariant mean pooling.
            - ``"sum"`` — cumulative sum (sensitive to degree).
            - ``"max"`` — element-wise maximum (saliency filtering).
            - ``"concat"`` — concatenation up to ``max_degree`` neighbors
              (fixed-size; order is arbitrary).

        message_dim: Dimensionality ``M`` of each message.  Inferred
            from the first entry of ``messages`` if omitted.

    Returns:
        Dict mapping ``"agent_i"`` to the aggregated neighbor message
        array of shape ``(M,)`` (or ``(M * k,)`` for ``"concat"``).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``aggregation`` is not one of the four supported
            operators.
    """
    adj = self.get_adjacency_matrix(agents)
    n = len(agents)

    # Infer message dimension M
    if message_dim is None:
        for val in messages.values():
            message_dim = val.shape[0]
            break
        if message_dim is None:
            message_dim = 1

    # Standardize message lookup
    msg_tensor = np.zeros((n, message_dim), dtype=np.float32)
    for i, a in enumerate(agents):
        if not a.alive:
            continue
        key_int = a.agent_id
        key_str = f"agent_{a.agent_id}"
        if key_int in messages:
            msg_tensor[i] = messages[key_int]
        elif key_str in messages:
            msg_tensor[i] = messages[key_str]

    inbox: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

    for i, agent in enumerate(agents):
        agent_key = f"agent_{agent.agent_id}"
        if not agent.alive:
            inbox[agent_key] = np.zeros(message_dim, dtype=np.float32)
            continue

        # In-neighbors of agent i: indices j where adj[i, j] > 0
        neighbor_indices = np.where(adj[i] > 0.5)[0]

        if len(neighbor_indices) == 0:
            # Isolated node or no alive neighbors
            inbox[agent_key] = np.zeros(message_dim, dtype=np.float32)
        else:
            neighbor_msgs = msg_tensor[neighbor_indices]  # (K, M)

            if aggregation == "mean":
                inbox[agent_key] = np.mean(neighbor_msgs, axis=0)
            elif aggregation == "sum":
                inbox[agent_key] = np.sum(neighbor_msgs, axis=0)
            elif aggregation == "max":
                inbox[agent_key] = np.max(neighbor_msgs, axis=0)
            elif aggregation == "concat":
                # Flatten up to max_degree neighbors
                inbox[agent_key] = neighbor_msgs.flatten()
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation: {aggregation}")

    return inbox

class ScrollSwarmEnv(ParallelEnv):
    """
    PettingZoo ``ParallelEnv`` implementation for cooperative UAV swarm reconnaissance.

    Each of the N drones receives a 16-dimensional continuous observation and
    chooses a discrete vertical action (UP / STAY / DOWN) simultaneously every
    step.  The environment supports centralized training with decentralized
    execution (CTDE) via ``state()`` and graph-neural-network (GNN) training
    via ``get_edge_index_and_attributes()``.

    Attributes:
        possible_agents: List of agent ID strings ``"agent_0"`` … ``"agent_{N-1}"``.
        agents: Currently active (non-terminated, non-truncated) agent IDs.
        metadata: PettingZoo metadata dict (``render_modes``, ``name``, ``render_fps``).
    """

    metadata = {
        "render_modes": ["human", "rgb_array"],
        "name": "scrollswarm_v0",
        "render_fps": 30,
    }

    def __init__(
        self,
        num_agents: int = 5,
        max_cycles: int = 1000,
        map_config: Optional[MapConfig] = None,
        comm_topology: Union[TopologyType, str] = TopologyType.CHAIN,
        target_reward: float = 1.0,
        crash_penalty: float = 10.0,
        step_reward: float = 0.01,
        team_reward: bool = False,
        render_mode: Optional[str] = None,
        backend: str = "auto",
    ):
        """
        Initializes the ScrollSwarm environment.

        Args:
            num_agents: Number of UAVs in the swarm. Must be in [1, 10].
            max_cycles: Maximum number of steps per episode before truncation.
            map_config: Corridor geometry and obstacle parameters. Defaults to
                ``MapConfig(width=800, height=400, fps=30)``.
            comm_topology: Graph topology for inter-drone message passing.
                One of ``"chain"``, ``"ring"``, ``"full"``, ``"radius"``,
                ``"capped"`` (or the equivalent ``TopologyType`` enum value).
            target_reward: Reward granted to each drone that contributes to a
                successful target photograph.
            crash_penalty: Penalty applied on boundary or obstacle collision
                (causes immediate individual termination).
            step_reward: Dense per-step survival incentive for living drones.
            team_reward: When ``True``, target rewards are shared equally among
                all living drones rather than awarded only to contributors.
            render_mode: ``"human"`` opens a live Pygame window; ``"rgb_array"``
                returns an ``(H, W, 3)`` uint8 NumPy image on each ``render()``
                call; ``None`` disables rendering entirely.
            backend: Geometric acceleration backend. Options: ``"auto"`` (fastest
                available on host), ``"numpy"`` (baseline), ``"numba"`` (LLVM JIT),
                or ``"cpp"`` (native C++20).

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``num_agents`` is outside [1, 10].
        """
        super().__init__()
        if not (1 <= num_agents <= 10):
            raise ValueError(f"num_agents must be between 1 and 10, got {num_agents}")

        self._num_agents = num_agents
        self.max_cycles = max_cycles
        self.map_config = map_config or MapConfig(width=800, height=400, fps=30)
        self.comm_topology = comm_topology
        self.comm_graph = CommunicationGraph(topology=comm_topology)
        self.target_reward = float(target_reward)
        self.crash_penalty = float(crash_penalty)
        self.step_reward = float(step_reward)
        self.team_reward = bool(team_reward)
        self.render_mode = render_mode
        self.backend = backend

        # Agent IDs conforming to PettingZoo standards
        self.possible_agents = [f"agent_{i}" for i in range(self._num_agents)]
        self.agents = self.possible_agents[:]

        # Pre-populate space dictionaries
        self.observation_spaces = {
            a: spaces.Box(low=-1.0, high=1.0, shape=(16,), dtype=np.float32)
            for a in self.possible_agents
        }
        self.action_spaces = {a: spaces.Discrete(3) for a in self.possible_agents}

        # Step counter for truncation
        self.step_count = 0

        # Physical map engine & agent entities
        self.scrolling_map = ScrollingMap(self.map_config)
        self._agent_map: Dict[str, Agent] = {}

        # Pygame rendering attributes (lazy initialized)
        self._pygame_initialized = False
        self._screen = None
        self._clock = None
        self._font = None
        self._id_font = None

        try:
            resolved_backend = resolve_backend(self.backend)
        except (ValueError, RuntimeError):
            resolved_backend = f"unresolved({self.backend})"

        logger.info(
            "Initialized ScrollSwarmEnv (agents=%d, max_cycles=%d, topology=%s, "
            "team_reward=%s, backend=%s->%s, render_mode=%s)",
            self._num_agents,
            self.max_cycles,
            self.comm_graph.topology.value,
            self.team_reward,
            self.backend,
            resolved_backend,
            self.render_mode,
        )

    @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
    def observation_space(self, agent: str) -> gym.Space:
        """
        Returns the observation space for the given agent.

        Each drone observes a 16-dimensional continuous feature vector bounded
        in ``[-1.0, 1.0]``.  The layout is:

        - **[0]** Normalized altitude ``y / H``
        - **[1–7]** LiDAR obstacle distances (7 rays, 120° FOV)
        - **[8–11]** Nearest-target relative vector ``[dx/W, dy/H, dist/diag, in_range]``
        - **[12–15]** Nearest-neighbor relative vector ``[dx/W, dy/H, dist/diag, in_comm]``

        Args:
            agent: PettingZoo agent ID string (e.g. ``"agent_0"``).

        Returns:
            ``spaces.Box(low=-1.0, high=1.0, shape=(16,), dtype=np.float32)``
        """
        return spaces.Box(
            low=-1.0,
            high=1.0,
            shape=(16,),
            dtype=np.float32,
        )

    @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
    def action_space(self, agent: str) -> gym.Space:
        """
        Returns the action space for the given agent.

        Args:
            agent: PettingZoo agent ID string (e.g. ``"agent_0"``).

        Returns:
            ``spaces.Discrete(3)`` mapping to
            ``{0: Action.UP, 1: Action.STAY, 2: Action.DOWN}``.
        """
        return spaces.Discrete(3)

    @property
    def state_space(self) -> gym.Space:
        """
        Centralized state space for CTDE algorithms (MAPPO, QMIX, MADDPG).

        Returns:
            ``spaces.Box`` of shape ``(16 * num_agents,)``, the concatenation of
            all agents' 16-dimensional observation vectors, bounded in
            ``[-1.0, 1.0]``.
        """
        total_dim = 16 * self._num_agents
        return spaces.Box(
            low=-1.0,
            high=1.0,
            shape=(total_dim,),
            dtype=np.float32,
        )

    def state(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Returns the centralized global state vector for CTDE.

        Concatenates the 16-dimensional observation of each possible agent in
        order.  Terminated agents (``alive == False``) contribute a zero vector
        of shape ``(16,)`` so the state dimension stays fixed at
        ``16 * num_agents``.

        Returns:
            ``np.ndarray`` of shape ``(16 * num_agents,)``, dtype ``float32``.
        """
        parts = []
        all_agents = list(self._agent_map.values())
        for agent_id in self.possible_agents:
            agent = self._agent_map.get(agent_id)
            if agent is not None and agent.alive:
                obs = agent.get_observation(self.scrolling_map, other_agents=all_agents)
            else:
                obs = np.zeros(16, dtype=np.float32)
            parts.append(obs)
        return np.concatenate(parts, dtype=np.float32)

    def reset(
        self,
        seed: Optional[int] = None,
        options: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    ) -> Tuple[Dict[str, np.ndarray], Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]]:
        """
        Resets the environment for a new episode.

        Regenerates the scrolling corridor, repositions all UAVs in evenly
        spaced vertical columns, and returns initial observations and telemetry.

        Args:
            seed: Optional integer seed for deterministic corridor generation
                and obstacle placement.
            options: Unused; accepted for PettingZoo API compatibility.

        Returns:
            observations: Dict mapping each agent ID to its initial
                16-dimensional observation array.
            infos: Dict mapping each agent ID to its initial telemetry dict
                ``{"targets_photographed": 0, "targets_collected": 0,
                "collision": None, "steps_alive": 0}``.
        """
        self.step_count = 0
        self.agents = self.possible_agents[:]

        logger.debug(
            "Reset ScrollSwarmEnv (seed=%s, num_agents=%d, backend=%s)",
            seed,
            self._num_agents,
            self.backend,
        )

        # Reset scrolling map with provided seed
        self.scrolling_map.reset(seed=seed)

        # Re-create internal agent entities centered in corridor
        agent_list = create_agents(
            num_agents=self._num_agents,
            map_width=self.scrolling_map.width,
            scrolling_map=self.scrolling_map,
            step_size=5,
            backend=self.backend,
        )
        self._agent_map = {f"agent_{i}": agent_list[i] for i in range(self._num_agents)}

        # Build initial observations and telemetry infos
        all_agents = list(self._agent_map.values())
        observations = {
            a: self._agent_map[a].get_observation(
                self.scrolling_map, other_agents=all_agents
            )
            for a in self.agents
        }
        infos = {
            a: {
                "targets_photographed": 0,
                "targets_collected": 0,
                "collision": None,
                "steps_alive": 0,
            }
            for a in self.agents
        }

        return observations, infos

    def step(
        self,
        actions: Dict[str, int],
    ) -> Tuple[
        Dict[str, np.ndarray],
        Dict[str, float],
        Dict[str, bool],
        Dict[str, bool],
        Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]],
    ]:
        """
        Executes one synchronized multi-agent step.

        The step proceeds in the following order:

        1. Applies discrete vertical actions for all living UAVs.
        2. Advances the scrolling map (obstacles and targets shift left).
        3. Checks boundary and obstacle collisions — collision causes immediate
           individual termination and applies ``crash_penalty``.
        4. Evaluates stochastic target inspection for all living drones within
           photo radius; successful photos grant ``target_reward``.
        5. Checks episode truncation at ``max_cycles``.
        6. Builds and returns PettingZoo-standard output dictionaries.

        Args:
            actions: Dict mapping each active agent ID to an integer action
                ``{0: UP, 1: STAY, 2: DOWN}``.

        Returns:
            observations: Post-step 16-dimensional observation for each agent.
            rewards: Per-agent scalar reward for this step.
            terminations: ``True`` for agents that collided this step.
            truncations: ``True`` for all agents when ``max_cycles`` is reached.
            infos: Per-agent telemetry ``{"targets_photographed": int,
                "targets_collected": int, "collision": str | None,
                "steps_alive": int}``.
        """
        self.step_count += 1
        rewards: Dict[str, float] = {a: 0.0 for a in self.agents}
        terminations: Dict[str, bool] = {a: False for a in self.agents}
        truncations: Dict[str, bool] = {a: False for a in self.agents}
        infos: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {a: {} for a in self.agents}

        # 1. Execute vertical movement actions
        for agent_id in self.agents:
            if agent_id in actions:
                action = actions[agent_id]
                self._agent_map[agent_id].step(action, self.scrolling_map.height)

        # 2. Advance scrolling map
        self.scrolling_map.step()

        # 3. Collision checks (instant structural termination on obstacle/boundary contact)
        for agent_id in self.agents:
            agent = self._agent_map[agent_id]
            collision_cause = None

            if agent.check_collision_boundary(self.scrolling_map):
                collision_cause = "boundary"
            elif agent.check_collision_obstacles(self.scrolling_map.obstacles):
                collision_cause = "obstacle"

            if collision_cause is not None:
                terminations[agent_id] = True
                rewards[agent_id] -= self.crash_penalty
                infos[agent_id]["collision"] = collision_cause
            else:
                infos[agent_id]["collision"] = None
                rewards[agent_id] += self.step_reward

        # 4. Stochastic target inspection under action uncertainty
        # Evaluate all targets against living drones
        living_agents = [
            self._agent_map[a] for a in self.agents if self._agent_map[a].alive
        ]
        targets_photographed_this_step = 0
        for target in self.scrolling_map.targets:
            if target.collected:
                continue
            if target.sample_inspection(living_agents, self.scrolling_map.rng):
                targets_photographed_this_step += 1
                # Find which drones contributed to the photo
                contributing_drones = [
                    d
                    for d in living_agents
                    if np.sqrt((d.x - target.x) ** 2 + (d.y - target.y) ** 2)
                    <= target.inspection_radius
                ]
                for d in contributing_drones:
                    d.score += 1

                if self.team_reward and living_agents:
                    team_share = self.target_reward / len(living_agents)
                    for d in living_agents:
                        rewards[f"agent_{d.agent_id}"] += team_share
                else:
                    for d in contributing_drones:
                        rewards[f"agent_{d.agent_id}"] += self.target_reward

        # 6. Check episode truncation
        is_truncated = self.step_count >= self.max_cycles
        for agent_id in self.agents:
            truncations[agent_id] = is_truncated
            agent = self._agent_map[agent_id]
            infos[agent_id]["targets_photographed"] = agent.score
            infos[agent_id]["targets_collected"] = agent.score  # Backward compatibility
            infos[agent_id]["steps_alive"] = agent.steps_alive

        # 7. Build observation vectors
        all_agents = list(self._agent_map.values())
        observations: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {
            a: self._agent_map[a].get_observation(
                self.scrolling_map, other_agents=all_agents
            )
            for a in self.agents
        }

        # 8. Cull terminated or truncated agents from active list
        self.agents = [
            a for a in self.agents if not terminations[a] and not truncations[a]
        ]

        return observations, rewards, terminations, truncations, infos

    def render(self) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:
        """
        Renders the aerial survey corridor.
        In 'human' mode: updates live Pygame display window.
        In 'rgb_array' mode: returns an (H, W, 3) uint8 NumPy image array.
        """
        if self.render_mode is None:
            return None

        if not self._pygame_initialized:
            import pygame

            pygame.init()
            if self.render_mode == "human":
                self._screen = pygame.display.set_mode(
                    (self.map_config.width, self.map_config.height)
                )
                pygame.display.set_caption("ScrollSwarm - UAV Swarm Reconnaissance")
            else:
                self._screen = pygame.Surface(
                    (self.map_config.width, self.map_config.height)
                )
            self._clock = pygame.time.Clock()
            self._font = pygame.font.SysFont("Consolas", 13)
            self._id_font = pygame.font.SysFont("Consolas", 10, bold=True)
            self._pygame_initialized = True

        import pygame

        w = self.scrolling_map.width
        h = self.scrolling_map.height

        # A. Airspace background & survey grid
        self._screen.fill(COLOR_AIRSPACE)
        for offset_lane in (60, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360):
            pygame.draw.line(
                self._screen,
                COLOR_GRID_LINE,
                (0, offset_lane),
                (w, offset_lane),
                width=1,
            )

        # B. Ceiling and Ground boundaries
        ceil_y = int(self.scrolling_map.ceiling_y)
        floor_y = int(self.scrolling_map.floor_y)
        pygame.draw.rect(self._screen, COLOR_CEILING, (0, 0, w, ceil_y))
        pygame.draw.rect(self._screen, COLOR_GROUND, (0, floor_y, w, h - floor_y))
        pygame.draw.line(self._screen, COLOR_BOUNDARY_RIM, (0, ceil_y), (w, ceil_y), 2)
        pygame.draw.line(
            self._screen, COLOR_BOUNDARY_RIM, (0, floor_y), (w, floor_y), 2
        )

        # C. Multi-scale obstacles (buildings, overhead towers, floating hazards)
        for obs in self.scrolling_map.obstacles:
            verts = [(int(vx), int(vy)) for vx, vy in obs.vertices]
            if len(verts) >= 3:
                fill_color = (
                    COLOR_HAZARD_FILL
                    if obs.obstacle_type == ObstacleType.FLOATING
                    else COLOR_BUILDING_FILL
                )
                edge_color = (
                    COLOR_HAZARD_OUTLINE
                    if obs.obstacle_type == ObstacleType.FLOATING
                    else COLOR_BUILDING_OUTLINE
                )
                pygame.draw.polygon(self._screen, fill_color, verts)
                pygame.draw.polygon(self._screen, edge_color, verts, width=2)
                if obs.obstacle_type != ObstacleType.FLOATING:
                    pygame.draw.line(
                        self._screen, COLOR_BUILDING_SPECULAR, verts[0], verts[2], 1
                    )

        # D. Inspection targets (with photo radius halos)
        for tgt in self.scrolling_map.targets:
            cx, cy, s = int(tgt.x), int(tgt.y), tgt.size
            if tgt.collected:
                pygame.draw.circle(self._screen, COLOR_TARGET_INSPECTED, (cx, cy), s)
                pygame.draw.circle(self._screen, (255, 255, 255), (cx, cy), 2)
            else:
                # Translucent photo inspection radius ring
                pygame.draw.circle(
                    self._screen,
                    (255, 215, 0),
                    (cx, cy),
                    int(tgt.inspection_radius),
                    width=1,
                )
                pygame.draw.circle(self._screen, COLOR_TARGET, (cx, cy), s)
                pygame.draw.circle(
                    self._screen, (255, 240, 150), (cx, cy), s + 3, width=1
                )
                pygame.draw.circle(self._screen, (255, 255, 255), (cx, cy), 2)

        # E. Communication graph links
        living_agents = [
            self._agent_map[a] for a in self.possible_agents if self._agent_map[a].alive
        ]
        comm_edges = self.comm_graph.get_communication_edges(living_agents)
        for p1, p2 in comm_edges:
            pygame.draw.line(
                self._screen,
                (70, 140, 230),
                (int(p1[0]), int(p1[1])),
                (int(p2[0]), int(p2[1])),
                1,
            )

        # F. UAV Quadcopters
        for agent_id in self.possible_agents:
            agent = self._agent_map[agent_id]
            color = agent.color if agent.alive else COLOR_AGENT_DEAD
            sprite = get_quadcopter_sprite(color, size=(24, 24))
            sw, sh = sprite.get_size()
            self._screen.blit(sprite, (int(agent.x - sw // 2), int(agent.y - sh // 2)))

            # Agent ID label
            tag_surf = self._id_font.render(
                f"#{agent.agent_id + 1}", True, (255, 255, 255)
            )
            self._screen.blit(
                tag_surf, (int(agent.x - tag_surf.get_width() // 2), int(agent.y - 18))
            )

        # Update display or export rgb array
        if self.render_mode == "human":
            pygame.event.pump()
            pygame.display.flip()

def __init__(
    self,
    num_agents: int = 5,
    max_cycles: int = 1000,
    map_config: Optional[MapConfig] = None,
    comm_topology: Union[TopologyType, str] = TopologyType.CHAIN,
    target_reward: float = 1.0,
    crash_penalty: float = 10.0,
    step_reward: float = 0.01,
    team_reward: bool = False,
    render_mode: Optional[str] = None,
    backend: str = "auto",
):
    """
    Initializes the ScrollSwarm environment.

    Args:
        num_agents: Number of UAVs in the swarm. Must be in [1, 10].
        max_cycles: Maximum number of steps per episode before truncation.
        map_config: Corridor geometry and obstacle parameters. Defaults to
            ``MapConfig(width=800, height=400, fps=30)``.
        comm_topology: Graph topology for inter-drone message passing.
            One of ``"chain"``, ``"ring"``, ``"full"``, ``"radius"``,
            ``"capped"`` (or the equivalent ``TopologyType`` enum value).
        target_reward: Reward granted to each drone that contributes to a
            successful target photograph.
        crash_penalty: Penalty applied on boundary or obstacle collision
            (causes immediate individual termination).
        step_reward: Dense per-step survival incentive for living drones.
        team_reward: When ``True``, target rewards are shared equally among
            all living drones rather than awarded only to contributors.
        render_mode: ``"human"`` opens a live Pygame window; ``"rgb_array"``
            returns an ``(H, W, 3)`` uint8 NumPy image on each ``render()``
            call; ``None`` disables rendering entirely.
        backend: Geometric acceleration backend. Options: ``"auto"`` (fastest
            available on host), ``"numpy"`` (baseline), ``"numba"`` (LLVM JIT),
            or ``"cpp"`` (native C++20).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``num_agents`` is outside [1, 10].
    """
    super().__init__()
    if not (1 <= num_agents <= 10):
        raise ValueError(f"num_agents must be between 1 and 10, got {num_agents}")

    self._num_agents = num_agents
    self.max_cycles = max_cycles
    self.map_config = map_config or MapConfig(width=800, height=400, fps=30)
    self.comm_topology = comm_topology
    self.comm_graph = CommunicationGraph(topology=comm_topology)
    self.target_reward = float(target_reward)
    self.crash_penalty = float(crash_penalty)
    self.step_reward = float(step_reward)
    self.team_reward = bool(team_reward)
    self.render_mode = render_mode
    self.backend = backend

    # Agent IDs conforming to PettingZoo standards
    self.possible_agents = [f"agent_{i}" for i in range(self._num_agents)]
    self.agents = self.possible_agents[:]

    # Pre-populate space dictionaries
    self.observation_spaces = {
        a: spaces.Box(low=-1.0, high=1.0, shape=(16,), dtype=np.float32)
        for a in self.possible_agents
    }
    self.action_spaces = {a: spaces.Discrete(3) for a in self.possible_agents}

    # Step counter for truncation
    self.step_count = 0

    # Physical map engine & agent entities
    self.scrolling_map = ScrollingMap(self.map_config)
    self._agent_map: Dict[str, Agent] = {}

    # Pygame rendering attributes (lazy initialized)
    self._pygame_initialized = False
    self._screen = None
    self._clock = None
    self._font = None
    self._id_font = None

    try:
        resolved_backend = resolve_backend(self.backend)
    except (ValueError, RuntimeError):
        resolved_backend = f"unresolved({self.backend})"

    logger.info(
        "Initialized ScrollSwarmEnv (agents=%d, max_cycles=%d, topology=%s, "
        "team_reward=%s, backend=%s->%s, render_mode=%s)",
        self._num_agents,
        self.max_cycles,
        self.comm_graph.topology.value,
        self.team_reward,
        self.backend,
        resolved_backend,
        self.render_mode,
    )

def render(self) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:
    """
    Renders the aerial survey corridor.
    In 'human' mode: updates live Pygame display window.
    In 'rgb_array' mode: returns an (H, W, 3) uint8 NumPy image array.
    """
    if self.render_mode is None:
        return None

    if not self._pygame_initialized:
        import pygame

        pygame.init()
        if self.render_mode == "human":
            self._screen = pygame.display.set_mode(
                (self.map_config.width, self.map_config.height)
            )
            pygame.display.set_caption("ScrollSwarm - UAV Swarm Reconnaissance")
        else:
            self._screen = pygame.Surface(
                (self.map_config.width, self.map_config.height)
            )
        self._clock = pygame.time.Clock()
        self._font = pygame.font.SysFont("Consolas", 13)
        self._id_font = pygame.font.SysFont("Consolas", 10, bold=True)
        self._pygame_initialized = True

    import pygame

    w = self.scrolling_map.width
    h = self.scrolling_map.height

    # A. Airspace background & survey grid
    self._screen.fill(COLOR_AIRSPACE)
    for offset_lane in (60, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360):
        pygame.draw.line(
            self._screen,
            COLOR_GRID_LINE,
            (0, offset_lane),
            (w, offset_lane),
            width=1,
        )

    # B. Ceiling and Ground boundaries
    ceil_y = int(self.scrolling_map.ceiling_y)
    floor_y = int(self.scrolling_map.floor_y)
    pygame.draw.rect(self._screen, COLOR_CEILING, (0, 0, w, ceil_y))
    pygame.draw.rect(self._screen, COLOR_GROUND, (0, floor_y, w, h - floor_y))
    pygame.draw.line(self._screen, COLOR_BOUNDARY_RIM, (0, ceil_y), (w, ceil_y), 2)
    pygame.draw.line(
        self._screen, COLOR_BOUNDARY_RIM, (0, floor_y), (w, floor_y), 2
    )

    # C. Multi-scale obstacles (buildings, overhead towers, floating hazards)
    for obs in self.scrolling_map.obstacles:
        verts = [(int(vx), int(vy)) for vx, vy in obs.vertices]
        if len(verts) >= 3:
            fill_color = (
                COLOR_HAZARD_FILL
                if obs.obstacle_type == ObstacleType.FLOATING
                else COLOR_BUILDING_FILL
            )
            edge_color = (
                COLOR_HAZARD_OUTLINE
                if obs.obstacle_type == ObstacleType.FLOATING
                else COLOR_BUILDING_OUTLINE
            )
            pygame.draw.polygon(self._screen, fill_color, verts)
            pygame.draw.polygon(self._screen, edge_color, verts, width=2)
            if obs.obstacle_type != ObstacleType.FLOATING:
                pygame.draw.line(
                    self._screen, COLOR_BUILDING_SPECULAR, verts[0], verts[2], 1
                )

    # D. Inspection targets (with photo radius halos)
    for tgt in self.scrolling_map.targets:
        cx, cy, s = int(tgt.x), int(tgt.y), tgt.size
        if tgt.collected:
            pygame.draw.circle(self._screen, COLOR_TARGET_INSPECTED, (cx, cy), s)
            pygame.draw.circle(self._screen, (255, 255, 255), (cx, cy), 2)
        else:
            # Translucent photo inspection radius ring
            pygame.draw.circle(
                self._screen,
                (255, 215, 0),
                (cx, cy),
                int(tgt.inspection_radius),
                width=1,
            )
            pygame.draw.circle(self._screen, COLOR_TARGET, (cx, cy), s)
            pygame.draw.circle(
                self._screen, (255, 240, 150), (cx, cy), s + 3, width=1
            )
            pygame.draw.circle(self._screen, (255, 255, 255), (cx, cy), 2)

    # E. Communication graph links
    living_agents = [
        self._agent_map[a] for a in self.possible_agents if self._agent_map[a].alive
    ]
    comm_edges = self.comm_graph.get_communication_edges(living_agents)
    for p1, p2 in comm_edges:
        pygame.draw.line(
            self._screen,
            (70, 140, 230),
            (int(p1[0]), int(p1[1])),
            (int(p2[0]), int(p2[1])),
            1,
        )

    # F. UAV Quadcopters
    for agent_id in self.possible_agents:
        agent = self._agent_map[agent_id]
        color = agent.color if agent.alive else COLOR_AGENT_DEAD
        sprite = get_quadcopter_sprite(color, size=(24, 24))
        sw, sh = sprite.get_size()
        self._screen.blit(sprite, (int(agent.x - sw // 2), int(agent.y - sh // 2)))

        # Agent ID label
        tag_surf = self._id_font.render(
            f"#{agent.agent_id + 1}", True, (255, 255, 255)
        )
        self._screen.blit(
            tag_surf, (int(agent.x - tag_surf.get_width() // 2), int(agent.y - 18))
        )

    # Update display or export rgb array
    if self.render_mode == "human":
        pygame.event.pump()
        pygame.display.flip()
        self._clock.tick(self.metadata["render_fps"])
        return None
    elif self.render_mode == "rgb_array":
        # Pygame surface to NumPy uint8 array of shape (H, W, 3)
        img_array = pygame.surfarray.array3d(self._screen)
        return np.transpose(img_array, (1, 0, 2))

def reset(
    self,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
    options: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
) -> Tuple[Dict[str, np.ndarray], Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]]:
    """
    Resets the environment for a new episode.

    Regenerates the scrolling corridor, repositions all UAVs in evenly
    spaced vertical columns, and returns initial observations and telemetry.

    Args:
        seed: Optional integer seed for deterministic corridor generation
            and obstacle placement.
        options: Unused; accepted for PettingZoo API compatibility.

    Returns:
        observations: Dict mapping each agent ID to its initial
            16-dimensional observation array.
        infos: Dict mapping each agent ID to its initial telemetry dict
            ``{"targets_photographed": 0, "targets_collected": 0,
            "collision": None, "steps_alive": 0}``.
    """
    self.step_count = 0
    self.agents = self.possible_agents[:]

    logger.debug(
        "Reset ScrollSwarmEnv (seed=%s, num_agents=%d, backend=%s)",
        seed,
        self._num_agents,
        self.backend,
    )

    # Reset scrolling map with provided seed
    self.scrolling_map.reset(seed=seed)

    # Re-create internal agent entities centered in corridor
    agent_list = create_agents(
        num_agents=self._num_agents,
        map_width=self.scrolling_map.width,
        scrolling_map=self.scrolling_map,
        step_size=5,
        backend=self.backend,
    )
    self._agent_map = {f"agent_{i}": agent_list[i] for i in range(self._num_agents)}

    # Build initial observations and telemetry infos
    all_agents = list(self._agent_map.values())
    observations = {
        a: self._agent_map[a].get_observation(
            self.scrolling_map, other_agents=all_agents
        )
        for a in self.agents
    }
    infos = {
        a: {
            "targets_photographed": 0,
            "targets_collected": 0,
            "collision": None,
            "steps_alive": 0,
        }
        for a in self.agents
    }

    return observations, infos

def state(self) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Returns the centralized global state vector for CTDE.

    Concatenates the 16-dimensional observation of each possible agent in
    order.  Terminated agents (``alive == False``) contribute a zero vector
    of shape ``(16,)`` so the state dimension stays fixed at
    ``16 * num_agents``.

    Returns:
        ``np.ndarray`` of shape ``(16 * num_agents,)``, dtype ``float32``.
    """
    parts = []
    all_agents = list(self._agent_map.values())
    for agent_id in self.possible_agents:
        agent = self._agent_map.get(agent_id)
        if agent is not None and agent.alive:
            obs = agent.get_observation(self.scrolling_map, other_agents=all_agents)
        else:
            obs = np.zeros(16, dtype=np.float32)
        parts.append(obs)
    return np.concatenate(parts, dtype=np.float32)

def step(
    self,
    actions: Dict[str, int],
) -> Tuple[
    Dict[str, np.ndarray],
    Dict[str, float],
    Dict[str, bool],
    Dict[str, bool],
    Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]],
]:
    """
    Executes one synchronized multi-agent step.

    The step proceeds in the following order:

    1. Applies discrete vertical actions for all living UAVs.
    2. Advances the scrolling map (obstacles and targets shift left).
    3. Checks boundary and obstacle collisions — collision causes immediate
       individual termination and applies ``crash_penalty``.
    4. Evaluates stochastic target inspection for all living drones within
       photo radius; successful photos grant ``target_reward``.
    5. Checks episode truncation at ``max_cycles``.
    6. Builds and returns PettingZoo-standard output dictionaries.

    Args:
        actions: Dict mapping each active agent ID to an integer action
            ``{0: UP, 1: STAY, 2: DOWN}``.

    Returns:
        observations: Post-step 16-dimensional observation for each agent.
        rewards: Per-agent scalar reward for this step.
        terminations: ``True`` for agents that collided this step.
        truncations: ``True`` for all agents when ``max_cycles`` is reached.
        infos: Per-agent telemetry ``{"targets_photographed": int,
            "targets_collected": int, "collision": str | None,
            "steps_alive": int}``.
    """
    self.step_count += 1
    rewards: Dict[str, float] = {a: 0.0 for a in self.agents}
    terminations: Dict[str, bool] = {a: False for a in self.agents}
    truncations: Dict[str, bool] = {a: False for a in self.agents}
    infos: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {a: {} for a in self.agents}

    # 1. Execute vertical movement actions
    for agent_id in self.agents:
        if agent_id in actions:
            action = actions[agent_id]
            self._agent_map[agent_id].step(action, self.scrolling_map.height)

    # 2. Advance scrolling map
    self.scrolling_map.step()

    # 3. Collision checks (instant structural termination on obstacle/boundary contact)
    for agent_id in self.agents:
        agent = self._agent_map[agent_id]
        collision_cause = None

        if agent.check_collision_boundary(self.scrolling_map):
            collision_cause = "boundary"
        elif agent.check_collision_obstacles(self.scrolling_map.obstacles):
            collision_cause = "obstacle"

        if collision_cause is not None:
            terminations[agent_id] = True
            rewards[agent_id] -= self.crash_penalty
            infos[agent_id]["collision"] = collision_cause
        else:
            infos[agent_id]["collision"] = None
            rewards[agent_id] += self.step_reward

    # 4. Stochastic target inspection under action uncertainty
    # Evaluate all targets against living drones
    living_agents = [
        self._agent_map[a] for a in self.agents if self._agent_map[a].alive
    ]
    targets_photographed_this_step = 0
    for target in self.scrolling_map.targets:
        if target.collected:
            continue
        if target.sample_inspection(living_agents, self.scrolling_map.rng):
            targets_photographed_this_step += 1
            # Find which drones contributed to the photo
            contributing_drones = [
                d
                for d in living_agents
                if np.sqrt((d.x - target.x) ** 2 + (d.y - target.y) ** 2)
                <= target.inspection_radius
            ]
            for d in contributing_drones:
                d.score += 1

            if self.team_reward and living_agents:
                team_share = self.target_reward / len(living_agents)
                for d in living_agents:
                    rewards[f"agent_{d.agent_id}"] += team_share
            else:
                for d in contributing_drones:
                    rewards[f"agent_{d.agent_id}"] += self.target_reward

    # 6. Check episode truncation
    is_truncated = self.step_count >= self.max_cycles
    for agent_id in self.agents:
        truncations[agent_id] = is_truncated
        agent = self._agent_map[agent_id]
        infos[agent_id]["targets_photographed"] = agent.score
        infos[agent_id]["targets_collected"] = agent.score  # Backward compatibility
        infos[agent_id]["steps_alive"] = agent.steps_alive

    # 7. Build observation vectors
    all_agents = list(self._agent_map.values())
    observations: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {
        a: self._agent_map[a].get_observation(
            self.scrolling_map, other_agents=all_agents
        )
        for a in self.agents
    }

    # 8. Cull terminated or truncated agents from active list
    self.agents = [
        a for a in self.agents if not terminations[a] and not truncations[a]
    ]

    return observations, rewards, terminations, truncations, infos

docs.title: Architectural Overview
docs.text:
Raycasting and obstacle collision checks account for approximately \(79.3\%\) of execution time in raw Python. The scrollswarm.geometry subsystem provides pluggable computational backends:

  • numpy (Baseline): Pure Python / NumPy analytical geometry with zero build dependencies. Always available across all platforms.
  • numba (LLVM JIT): JIT-compiled native CPU machine code (@njit(fastmath=True, nogil=True)), offering \(50\times\) speedup on isolated raycasting without requiring a C++ compiler.
  • cpp (Native C++20 Extension): Pre-compiled native C++20 geometry kernel built via pybind11 with zero JIT warmup latency (\(33\times\) isolated raycasting speedup).
  • auto (Default): Automatically probes the host environment and selects the fastest available backend (priority: cpp \(\to\) numba \(\to\) numpy).

def resolve_backend(requested: str = "auto") -> str:
    """
    Resolves backend name against host system capabilities.

    Priority order for 'auto':
    1. 'cpp' (compiled native C++20 kernel)
    2. 'numba' (LLVM JIT CPU acceleration)
    3. 'numpy' (guaranteed portable fallback)
    """
    req = requested.lower().strip()
    if req == "auto":
        if is_cpp_available():
            return "cpp"
        if is_numba_available():
            return "numba"
        return "numpy"

    if req == "numba":
        if not is_numba_available():
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Numba backend requested, but 'numba' is not installed or import failed."
            )
        return "numba"

    if req == "cpp":
        if not is_cpp_available():
            raise RuntimeError(
                "C++ geometry backend requested, but 'scrollswarm._geometry_cpp' is not compiled."
            )
        return "cpp"

    if req == "numpy":
        return "numpy"

    raise ValueError(
        f"Unknown geometry backend: '{requested}'. Valid options: ['auto', 'numpy', 'numba', 'cpp']."
    )

def extract_geometry_buffers(
    obstacles: List[object],
    targets: List[object],
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Extracts contiguous flat NumPy arrays from scrolling map entities
    for zero-overhead vectorized / JIT geometry kernels.

    Returns:
        obs_meta:        (N_obs, 4) float32 - [x, y, radius, max_dim]
        obs_edges:       (N_edges, 4) float32 - [ax, ay, bx, by]
        obs_edge_ranges: (N_obs, 2) int32 - [start_idx, end_idx]
        target_data:     (N_tgts, 3) float32 - [x, y, radius]
    """
    n_obs = len(obstacles)
    obs_meta = np.zeros((n_obs, 4), dtype=np.float32)
    obs_edge_ranges = np.zeros((n_obs, 2), dtype=np.int32)

    all_edges: List[Tuple[float, float, float, float]] = []

    for i, obs in enumerate(obstacles):
        ox = float(getattr(obs, "x", 0.0))
        oy = float(getattr(obs, "y", 0.0))
        radius = float(getattr(obs, "radius", 20.0))
        max_dim = float(
            max(
                radius,
                getattr(obs, "width", 40.0),
                getattr(obs, "height", 60.0),
            )
        )
        obs_meta[i] = [ox, oy, radius, max_dim]

        start_e = len(all_edges)
        edges = getattr(obs, "edges", [])
        for (ax, ay), (bx, by) in edges:
            all_edges.append((float(ax), float(ay), float(bx), float(by)))
        end_e = len(all_edges)
        obs_edge_ranges[i] = [start_e, end_e]

    if all_edges:
        obs_edges = np.array(all_edges, dtype=np.float32)
    else:
        obs_edges = np.zeros((0, 4), dtype=np.float32)

    # Active targets
    active_tgts = [t for t in targets if not getattr(t, "collected", False)]
    n_tgts = len(active_tgts)
    target_data = np.zeros((n_tgts, 3), dtype=np.float32)
    for j, tgt in enumerate(active_tgts):
        tx = float(getattr(tgt, "x", 0.0))
        ty = float(getattr(tgt, "y", 0.0))
        tr = float(getattr(tgt, "size", 16.0))
        target_data[j] = [tx, ty, tr]

    return obs_meta, obs_edges, obs_edge_ranges, target_data

class ScrollingMap:
    """
    Manages the scrolling aerial corridor, multi-scale procedural obstacles,
    guaranteed navigable passage, and stochastic inspection targets.

    The map advances one pixel per step (``scroll_speed = 1``) in the leftward
    direction.  Obstacles are procedurally generated off-screen to the right
    and culled when they scroll past the left edge.  The minimum navigable gap
    ``G_min >= min_corridor_gap`` is enforced at spawn time.

    Attributes:
        config: ``MapConfig`` instance governing all corridor parameters.
        width: Corridor width in pixels.
        height: Corridor height in pixels.
        ceiling_y: Upper navigable boundary ``y`` in pixels.
        floor_y: Lower navigable boundary ``y`` in pixels.
        obstacles: List of active ``Obstacle`` polygon entities.
        targets: List of active ``Target`` waypoint entities.
        rng: ``numpy.random.Generator`` used for all stochastic decisions.
        global_step: Monotonically increasing step counter.
        top_heights: Per-column ceiling boundary array (shape ``(W,)``).
        bot_heights: Per-column floor inset array (shape ``(W,)``).
    """

    def __init__(self, config: Optional[MapConfig] = None):
        """
        Initializes the ScrollingMap.

        Args:
            config: ``MapConfig`` dataclass instance.  Defaults to
                ``MapConfig()`` (800×400 corridor, standard spawn rates).
        """
        self.config = config or MapConfig()
        self.width = self.config.width
        self.height = self.config.height
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(self.config.seed)

        self.min_corridor_gap = self.config.min_corridor_gap
        self.ceiling_y = self.config.ceiling_y
        self.floor_y = self.height - self.config.floor_margin
        self.global_step: int = 0

        # Boundary arrays (for backward compatibility with column-based checks)
        self.top_heights = np.full(self.width, self.ceiling_y, dtype=np.float32)
        self.bot_heights = np.full(
            self.width, self.config.floor_margin, dtype=np.float32
        )

        # Active dynamic entities
        self.obstacles: List[Obstacle] = []
        self.targets: List[Target] = []

        # Spawning timers
        self._steps_since_obstacle = 40
        self._steps_since_target = 30

        # Cached contiguous geometry buffers for current step
        self._geo_cache: Optional[
            Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
        ] = None

        if getattr(self.config, "preseed", True):
            self._preseed_corridor()

    def reset(self, seed: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
        """Resets the map state, entities, and random number generator."""
        if seed is not None:
            self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        self.global_step = 0
        self._steps_since_obstacle = 40
        self._steps_since_target = 30
        self.obstacles.clear()
        self.targets.clear()
        self._geo_cache = None
        if getattr(self.config, "preseed", True):
            self._preseed_corridor()

    def _create_ground_structure(self, spawn_x: float, max_h: float) -> Obstacle:
        """Creates a ground-standing building or tower."""
        width = float(self.rng.uniform(30.0, 70.0))
        h = float(self.rng.uniform(40.0, max(50.0, max_h)))
        center_y = float(self.floor_y - h / 2.0)
        return Obstacle(
            x=float(spawn_x),
            y=center_y,
            base_y=center_y,
            width=width,
            height=h,
            obstacle_type=ObstacleType.STRUCTURE,
            vx=1.0,
        )

    def _create_overhead_structure(self, spawn_x: float, max_depth: float) -> Obstacle:
        """Creates an overhead suspended structure extending down from the ceiling."""
        width = float(self.rng.uniform(30.0, 70.0))
        depth = float(self.rng.uniform(30.0, max(40.0, max_depth)))
        center_y = float(self.ceiling_y + depth / 2.0)
        return Obstacle(
            x=float(spawn_x),
            y=center_y,
            base_y=center_y,
            width=width,
            height=depth,
            obstacle_type=ObstacleType.OVERHEAD,
            vx=1.0,
        )

    def _create_floating_hazard(self, spawn_x: float) -> Obstacle:
        """Creates a mid-air polygonal floating hazard with subtle epicyclic oscillation."""
        radius = float(self.rng.uniform(14.0, 32.0))
        vy_amp = float(self.rng.uniform(4.0, 16.0))
        omega = float(self.rng.uniform(0.02, 0.06))
        phase = float(self.rng.uniform(0.0, 2 * np.pi))

        effective_h = radius + vy_amp
        y_min = self.ceiling_y + effective_h + 15.0
        y_max = self.floor_y - effective_h - 15.0

        if y_min >= y_max:
            base_y = float(self.height / 2.0)
            vy_amp = 0.0
        else:
            base_y = float(self.rng.uniform(y_min, y_max))

        return Obstacle(
            x=float(spawn_x),
            y=base_y,
            base_y=base_y,
            radius=radius,
            width=radius * 2.0,
            height=radius * 2.0,
            obstacle_type=ObstacleType.FLOATING,
            vx=1.0,
            vy_amplitude=vy_amp,
            omega=omega,
            phase=phase,
        )

    def _create_procedural_obstacle(self, spawn_x: float) -> Obstacle:
        """
        Samples an obstacle type (ground structure, overhead structure, or floating hazard)
        while strictly preserving the guaranteed navigable corridor gap (>= 110 px).
        """
        max_structure_h = (self.floor_y - self.ceiling_y) - self.min_corridor_gap - 10.0
        max_structure_h = max(35.0, max_structure_h)

        obs_kind = self.rng.choice(
            [ObstacleType.STRUCTURE, ObstacleType.OVERHEAD, ObstacleType.FLOATING],
            p=[0.45, 0.35, 0.20],
        )

        if obs_kind == ObstacleType.STRUCTURE:
            return self._create_ground_structure(spawn_x, max_structure_h)
        elif obs_kind == ObstacleType.OVERHEAD:
            return self._create_overhead_structure(spawn_x, max_structure_h)
        else:
            return self._create_floating_hazard(spawn_x)

    def _preseed_corridor(self) -> None:
        """Populates the initial corridor with starting obstacles and inspection targets."""
        if self.width < 250 or self.height < 120:
            return

        x_positions = [self.width * 0.35, self.width * 0.60, self.width * 0.82]
        for x in x_positions:
            self.obstacles.append(self._create_procedural_obstacle(x))

        target_positions = [self.width * 0.45, self.width * 0.70, self.width * 0.92]
        for x in target_positions:
            low_y = min(self.ceiling_y + 35.0, self.height / 2.0 - 10.0)
            high_y = max(self.floor_y - 35.0, self.height / 2.0 + 10.0)
            if high_y <= low_y:
                high_y = low_y + 10.0
            y = float(self.rng.uniform(low_y, high_y))
            self.targets.append(Target(x=x, y=y))

    def step(self) -> None:
        """Advances the simulation by 1 step: updates obstacles, targets, and handles spawning."""
        self.global_step += 1
        self._steps_since_obstacle += 1
        self._steps_since_target += 1

        # 1. Advance dynamic obstacles
        for obs in self.obstacles:
            obs.step()

        # 2. Advance targets
        for tgt in self.targets:
            tgt.step()

        # 3. Cull offscreen entities
        self.obstacles = [obs for obs in self.obstacles if not obs.is_offscreen]
        self.targets = [tgt for tgt in self.targets if not tgt.is_offscreen]

        # 4. Stochastic spawning at right edge
        if self._steps_since_obstacle >= self.config.obstacle_spawn_interval:
            if self.rng.random() < 0.40:
                spawn_x = float(self.width + self.rng.uniform(30.0, 70.0))
                self.obstacles.append(self._create_procedural_obstacle(spawn_x))
                self._steps_since_obstacle = 0

        if self._steps_since_target >= self.config.target_spawn_interval:
            if self.rng.random() < 0.35:
                spawn_x = float(self.width + self.rng.uniform(20.0, 50.0))
                low_y = min(self.ceiling_y + 35.0, self.height / 2.0 - 10.0)
                high_y = max(self.floor_y - 35.0, self.height / 2.0 + 10.0)
                if high_y <= low_y:
                    high_y = low_y + 10.0
                y = float(self.rng.uniform(low_y, high_y))
                self.targets.append(Target(x=spawn_x, y=y))
                self._steps_since_target = 0

        # Invalidate geometry buffer cache on step
        self._geo_cache = None

    def get_geometry_buffers(
        self,
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Returns cached contiguous NumPy geometry buffers for current map step."""
        if self._geo_cache is None:
            from scrollswarm.geometry import extract_geometry_buffers

            self._geo_cache = extract_geometry_buffers(self.obstacles, self.targets)
        return self._geo_cache

    def update(self) -> None:
        """Alias for step()."""
        self.step()

    # Backward compatibility aliases
    @property
    def asteroids(self) -> List[Obstacle]:
        return self.obstacles

    @asteroids.setter
    def asteroids(self, val: List[Obstacle]) -> None:
        self.obstacles = val

    @property
    def trees(self) -> List[Obstacle]:
        return self.obstacles

    @trees.setter
    def trees(self, val: List[Obstacle]) -> None:
        self.obstacles = val
