def step(self) -> None:
    """Advances the simulation by 1 step: updates obstacles, targets, and handles spawning."""
    self.global_step += 1
    self._steps_since_obstacle += 1
    self._steps_since_target += 1

    # 1. Advance dynamic obstacles
    for obs in self.obstacles:
        obs.step()

    # 2. Advance targets
    for tgt in self.targets:
        tgt.step()

    # 3. Cull offscreen entities
    self.obstacles = [obs for obs in self.obstacles if not obs.is_offscreen]
    self.targets = [tgt for tgt in self.targets if not tgt.is_offscreen]

    # 4. Stochastic spawning at right edge
    if self._steps_since_obstacle >= self.config.obstacle_spawn_interval:
        if self.rng.random() < 0.40:
            spawn_x = float(self.width + self.rng.uniform(30.0, 70.0))
            self.obstacles.append(self._create_procedural_obstacle(spawn_x))
            self._steps_since_obstacle = 0

    if self._steps_since_target >= self.config.target_spawn_interval:
        if self.rng.random() < 0.35:
            spawn_x = float(self.width + self.rng.uniform(20.0, 50.0))
            low_y = min(self.ceiling_y + 35.0, self.height / 2.0 - 10.0)
            high_y = max(self.floor_y - 35.0, self.height / 2.0 + 10.0)
            if high_y <= low_y:
                high_y = low_y + 10.0
            y = float(self.rng.uniform(low_y, high_y))
            self.targets.append(Target(x=spawn_x, y=y))
            self._steps_since_target = 0

    # Invalidate geometry buffer cache on step
    self._geo_cache = None

@dataclass
class Obstacle:
    """
    A multi-scale 2D obstacle (ground structure, overhead barrier, or floating hazard).
    Modeled as an arbitrary convex polygon with drift velocity and optional oscillation:
        x(t) = x_0 - v_x * t
        y(t) = y_base + A * sin(omega * t + phase)
    """

    x: float
    y: float
    base_y: float = 0.0
    radius: float = 20.0
    width: float = 40.0
    height: float = 60.0
    obstacle_type: ObstacleType = ObstacleType.STRUCTURE
    vertices_rel: List[Tuple[float, float]] = field(default_factory=list)
    vx: float = 1.0
    vy_amplitude: float = 0.0
    omega: float = 0.0
    phase: float = 0.0
    step_count: int = 0

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.base_y == 0.0:
            self.base_y = self.y

        if not self.vertices_rel:
            if (
                self.obstacle_type == ObstacleType.STRUCTURE
                or self.obstacle_type == ObstacleType.OVERHEAD
            ):
                # Rectangular structure
                hw = self.width / 2.0
                hh = self.height / 2.0
                self.vertices_rel = [
                    (-hw, -hh),
                    (hw, -hh),
                    (hw, hh),
                    (-hw, hh),
                ]
                self.radius = float(np.sqrt(hw * hw + hh * hh))
            else:
                # Regular / irregular polygon for floating debris
                angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 7)[:-1]
                self.vertices_rel = [
                    (float(self.radius * np.cos(a)), float(self.radius * np.sin(a)))
                    for a in angles
                ]

    def step(self) -> None:
        """Advances the obstacle's horizontal drift and vertical oscillation."""
        self.x -= self.vx
        self.step_count += 1
        if self.vy_amplitude > 0.0:
            self.y = self.base_y + self.vy_amplitude * np.sin(
                self.omega * self.step_count + self.phase
            )

    @property
    def vertices(self) -> List[Tuple[float, float]]:
        """Returns the absolute 2D coordinates of the polygon's vertices."""
        return [(self.x + dx, self.y + dy) for dx, dy in self.vertices_rel]

    @property
    def edges(self) -> List[Tuple[Tuple[float, float], Tuple[float, float]]]:
        """Returns the consecutive edge line segments [(v0, v1), (v1, v2), ...]."""
        verts = self.vertices
        n = len(verts)
        return [(verts[i], verts[(i + 1) % n]) for i in range(n)]

    @property
    def is_offscreen(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the entire obstacle has scrolled past the left viewport edge."""
        if self.vertices_rel:
            max_rel_x = max(dx for dx, _ in self.vertices_rel)
            return self.x + max_rel_x < 0.0
        return self.x + self.radius < 0.0

    def contains_point(self, px: float, py: float) -> bool:
        """Determines if point (px, py) lies inside the polygon using ray-casting."""
        verts = self.vertices
        n = len(verts)
        if n == 0:
            return False
        inside = False
        p1x, p1y = verts[0]
        for i in range(n + 1):
            p2x, p2y = verts[i % n]
            if py > min(p1y, p2y):
                if py <= max(p1y, p2y):
                    if px <= max(p1x, p2x):
                        if p1y != p2y:
                            xinters = (py - p1y) * (p2x - p1x) / (p2y - p1y) + p1x
                        if p1x == p2x or px <= xinters:
                            inside = not inside
            p1x, p1y = p2x, p2y
        return inside

    def distance_to_point(self, px: float, py: float) -> float:
        """Computes minimum Euclidean distance from (px, py) to the polygon boundary."""
        if self.contains_point(px, py):
            return 0.0

        if not self.edges:
            dx = px - self.x
            dy = py - self.y
            return float(max(0.0, np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) - self.radius))

        min_dist_sq = float("inf")
        for (ax, ay), (bx, by) in self.edges:
            vx = bx - ax
            vy = by - ay
            wx = px - ax
            wy = py - ay
            c1 = wx * vx + wy * vy
            if c1 <= 0.0:
                dist_sq = (px - ax) ** 2 + (py - ay) ** 2
            else:
                c2 = vx * vx + vy * vy
                if c2 <= c1:
                    dist_sq = (px - bx) ** 2 + (py - by) ** 2
                else:
                    b = c1 / c2
                    proj_x = ax + b * vx
                    proj_y = ay + b * vy
                    dist_sq = (px - proj_x) ** 2 + (py - proj_y) ** 2
            if dist_sq < min_dist_sq:
                min_dist_sq = dist_sq

        return float(np.sqrt(min_dist_sq))

@dataclass
class Target:
    """
    An inspection target entity requiring aerial photography within an inspection radius.
    Action uncertainty is modeled via stochastic capture probability:
        P_j = (1 - d_j / D_photo) * sensor_reliability
        P_team = 1 - Prod_j (1 - P_j)
    """

    x: float
    y: float
    size: int = 8
    inspection_radius: float = 45.0
    sensor_reliability: float = 0.85
    collected: bool = False
    vx: float = 1.0

    def step(self) -> None:
        """Drifts with the base aerial corridor scroll."""
        self.x -= self.vx

    @property
    def is_offscreen(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the target has scrolled off the left edge."""
        return self.x + self.size < 0.0

    def sample_inspection(
        self,
        drones: List["Agent"],
        rng: np.random.Generator,
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Evaluates stochastic photo acquisition by nearby living drones within inspection radius.
        Returns True if a clear photograph is successfully captured.
        """
        if self.collected:
            return False

        # Gather nearby living drones
        inspecting_drones = []
        for drone in drones:
            if not drone.alive:
                continue
            dx = drone.x - self.x
            dy = drone.y - self.y
            dist = np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
            if dist <= self.inspection_radius:
                inspecting_drones.append(dist)

        if not inspecting_drones:
            return False

        # Probability of team success under action uncertainty
        p_fail_team = 1.0
        for dist in inspecting_drones:
            # Proximity factor: closer drones have higher capture probability
            p_drone = (1.0 - (dist / self.inspection_radius)) * self.sensor_reliability
            p_drone = float(np.clip(p_drone, 0.05, 0.95))
            p_fail_team *= 1.0 - p_drone

        p_success_team = 1.0 - p_fail_team
        if rng.random() < p_success_team:
            self.collected = True
            return True

        return False

class RaySensor:
    """
    Multi-modal perception sensor for a ScrollSwarm UAV.

    Combines three sensing modalities into one 16-dimensional observation:

    - **LiDAR rangefinder:** 7 rays spanning a 120° forward FOV, detecting
      corridor boundaries and polygon obstacles via exact analytic
      ray–edge intersection (vector cross-product).
    - **Target tracker:** Relative bearing and distance to the nearest
      uninspected waypoint target.
    - **Neighbor proximity sensor:** Relative bearing and distance to the
      nearest living teammate drone, plus a binary communication-range flag.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        num_rays: int = 7,
        max_range: float = 400.0,  # Default: forward half of 800px screen
        fov_degrees: float = 120.0,  # Spans -60° (up-forward) to +60° (down-forward)
        photo_radius: float = 45.0,
        comm_range: float = 180.0,
        safe_proximity_dist: float = 28.0,
        backend: str = "auto",
    ):
        """
        Initializes the RaySensor.

        Args:
            num_rays: Number of LiDAR rays cast per observation step.
                Default 7 covers the full 120° FOV at 20° increments.
            max_range: Maximum ray travel distance in pixels.  Rays that reach
                this limit without a hit report ``norm_distance = 1.0``.
            fov_degrees: Total angular span of the ray fan in degrees,
                centred on the forward (rightward) direction.  Default 120°
                spans −60° (up-forward) to +60° (down-forward).
            photo_radius: Maximum pixel distance at which a drone can photograph
                a target, used to compute the ``in_range`` flag in the
                observation vector.
            comm_range: Maximum pixel distance at which two drones are
                considered to be within communication range, used to compute
                the ``in_comm`` flag in the observation vector.
            safe_proximity_dist: Legacy parameter retained for backward
                compatibility with proximity-penalty code paths.
            backend: Acceleration backend for geometric raycasting. Options:
                ``"auto"`` (fastest available), ``"numpy"`` (baseline),
                ``"numba"`` (LLVM JIT), or ``"cpp"`` (native C++20).
        """
        self.num_rays = num_rays
        self.max_range = float(max_range)
        self.fov_degrees = float(fov_degrees)
        self.photo_radius = float(photo_radius)
        self.comm_range = float(comm_range)
        self.safe_proximity_dist = float(safe_proximity_dist)
        self.backend = backend

        # Compute ray angles (in radians), from top-forward to bottom-forward
        half_fov = np.radians(self.fov_degrees / 2.0)
        self.angles = np.linspace(-half_fov, half_fov, self.num_rays, dtype=np.float32)

    def cast_rays(
        self,
        origin_x: float,
        origin_y: float,
        scrolling_map: "ScrollingMap",
    ) -> Tuple[List[RayHit], List[RayHit]]:
        """
        Casts LiDAR rays from (origin_x, origin_y) using the configured geometry backend.
        Returns (obstacle_hits, target_hits).
        """
        obs_hits: List[RayHit] = []
        tgt_hits: List[RayHit] = []

        ceil_y = float(scrolling_map.ceiling_y)
        floor_y = float(scrolling_map.floor_y)

        obstacles = getattr(scrolling_map, "obstacles", [])
        if not obstacles and hasattr(scrolling_map, "asteroids"):
            obstacles = scrolling_map.asteroids
        targets = getattr(scrolling_map, "targets", [])

        if hasattr(scrolling_map, "get_geometry_buffers"):
            obs_meta, obs_edges, obs_edge_ranges, target_data = (
                scrolling_map.get_geometry_buffers()
            )
        else:
            obs_meta, obs_edges, obs_edge_ranges, target_data = (
                extract_geometry_buffers(obstacles, targets)
            )

        backend_name = resolve_backend(self.backend)
        if backend_name == "cpp" and is_cpp_available():
            obs_dists, obs_types, obs_ends, tgt_dists, tgt_types, tgt_ends = (
                cast_rays_cpp(
                    origin_x,
                    origin_y,
                    self.angles,
                    self.max_range,
                    ceil_y,
                    floor_y,
                    obs_meta,
                    obs_edges,
                    obs_edge_ranges,
                    target_data,
                )
            )
        elif backend_name == "numba" and is_numba_available():
            obs_dists, obs_types, obs_ends, tgt_dists, tgt_types, tgt_ends = (
                cast_rays_numba(
                    origin_x,
                    origin_y,
                    self.angles,
                    self.max_range,
                    ceil_y,
                    floor_y,
                    obs_meta,
                    obs_edges,
                    obs_edge_ranges,
                    target_data,
                )
            )
        else:
            obs_dists, obs_types, obs_ends, tgt_dists, tgt_types, tgt_ends = (
                cast_rays_numpy(
                    origin_x,
                    origin_y,
                    self.angles,
                    self.max_range,
                    ceil_y,
                    floor_y,
                    obs_meta,
                    obs_edges,
                    obs_edge_ranges,
                    target_data,
                )
            )

        obs_type_labels = {0: "none", 1: "boundary", 2: "obstacle"}
        tgt_type_labels = {0: "none", 1: "target"}

        for k in range(self.num_rays):
            d = float(obs_dists[k])
            obs_hits.append(
                RayHit(
                    distance=d,
                    norm_distance=d / self.max_range,
                    hit_type=obs_type_labels.get(int(obs_types[k]), "none"),
                    endpoint=(float(obs_ends[k, 0]), float(obs_ends[k, 1])),
                )
            )

            td = float(tgt_dists[k])
            tgt_hits.append(
                RayHit(
                    distance=td,
                    norm_distance=td / self.max_range,
                    hit_type=tgt_type_labels.get(int(tgt_types[k]), "none"),
                    endpoint=(float(tgt_ends[k, 0]), float(tgt_ends[k, 1])),
                )
            )

        return obs_hits, tgt_hits

    def observe(
        self,
        origin_x: float,
        origin_y: float,
        scrolling_map: "ScrollingMap",
        other_agents: Optional[List["Agent"]] = None,
        agent_id: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Constructs the complete 16-dimensional observation vector:
        - 1 float: self_y / H in [0.0, 1.0]
        - 7 floats: LiDAR obstacle normalized distances in [0.0, 1.0]
        - 4 floats: Nearest target [dx/W, dy/H, dist/diag, in_range]
        - 4 floats: Nearest neighbor [dx/W, dy/H, dist/diag, proximity_alert]
        """
        w = float(scrolling_map.width)
        h = float(scrolling_map.height)
        diag = float(np.sqrt(w * w + h * h))

        # 1. Normalized altitude
        self_y_norm = float(np.clip(origin_y / h, 0.0, 1.0))

        # 2. LiDAR rays
        obs_hits, _ = self.cast_rays(origin_x, origin_y, scrolling_map)
        obs_dists = [hit.norm_distance for hit in obs_hits]

        # 3. Nearest uninspected target vector
        nearest_tgt_dist = float("inf")
        target_vec = [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0]

        for tgt in scrolling_map.targets:
            if tgt.collected:
                continue
            dx = tgt.x - origin_x
            dy = tgt.y - origin_y
            d = float(np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy))
            if d < nearest_tgt_dist:
                nearest_tgt_dist = d
                in_range = 1.0 if d <= self.photo_radius else 0.0
                target_vec = [
                    float(np.clip(dx / w, -1.0, 1.0)),
                    float(np.clip(dy / h, -1.0, 1.0)),
                    float(np.clip(d / diag, 0.0, 1.0)),
                    in_range,
                ]

        # 4. Nearest living neighbor drone vector
        nearest_nbr_dist = float("inf")
        nbr_vec = [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0]

        if other_agents is not None:
            for other in other_agents:
                if not other.alive:
                    continue
                if agent_id is not None and other.agent_id == agent_id:
                    continue
                dx = other.x - origin_x
                dy = other.y - origin_y
                if abs(dx) < 1e-4 and abs(dy) < 1e-4:
                    continue
                d = float(np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy))
                if d < nearest_nbr_dist:
                    nearest_nbr_dist = d
                    in_comm = 1.0 if d <= self.comm_range else 0.0
                    nbr_vec = [
                        float(np.clip(dx / w, -1.0, 1.0)),
                        float(np.clip(dy / h, -1.0, 1.0)),
                        float(np.clip(d / diag, 0.0, 1.0)),
                        in_comm,
                    ]

        obs_array = np.array(
            [self_y_norm] + obs_dists + target_vec + nbr_vec, dtype=np.float32
        )
        return obs_array

    """
    Initializes the RaySensor.

    Args:
        num_rays: Number of LiDAR rays cast per observation step.
            Default 7 covers the full 120° FOV at 20° increments.
        max_range: Maximum ray travel distance in pixels.  Rays that reach
            this limit without a hit report ``norm_distance = 1.0``.
        fov_degrees: Total angular span of the ray fan in degrees,
            centred on the forward (rightward) direction.  Default 120°
            spans −60° (up-forward) to +60° (down-forward).
        photo_radius: Maximum pixel distance at which a drone can photograph
            a target, used to compute the ``in_range`` flag in the
            observation vector.
        comm_range: Maximum pixel distance at which two drones are
            considered to be within communication range, used to compute
            the ``in_comm`` flag in the observation vector.
        safe_proximity_dist: Legacy parameter retained for backward
            compatibility with proximity-penalty code paths.
        backend: Acceleration backend for geometric raycasting. Options:
            ``"auto"`` (fastest available), ``"numpy"`` (baseline),
            ``"numba"`` (LLVM JIT), or ``"cpp"`` (native C++20).
    """
    self.num_rays = num_rays
    self.max_range = float(max_range)
    self.fov_degrees = float(fov_degrees)
    self.photo_radius = float(photo_radius)
    self.comm_range = float(comm_range)
    self.safe_proximity_dist = float(safe_proximity_dist)
    self.backend = backend

    # Compute ray angles (in radians), from top-forward to bottom-forward
    half_fov = np.radians(self.fov_degrees / 2.0)
    self.angles = np.linspace(-half_fov, half_fov, self.num_rays, dtype=np.float32)

docs.title: Vectorized Environments API
docs.text:
The scrollswarm.vector module provides synchronous (SyncVectorScrollSwarm) and multiprocess parallel (AsyncVectorScrollSwarm) runners designed explicitly for CTDE and Graph-Based MARL training.

Unlike generic PettingZoo-to-Gymnasium vectorizers that flatten (E, N) into a single batch axis and discard .state() and graph topologies, scrollswarm.vector preserves swarm structure across all \(\mathcal{E}\) corridors.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Preserved Swarm Axes: Returns rectangular NumPy batches with explicit corridor (\(\mathcal{E}\)) and agent (\(N\)) dimensions (obs: (E, N, 16), rewards: (E, N), alive_mask: (E, N)).
  • CTDE Global State: Exposes centralized critic inputs (infos["state"] of shape (E, 16 * N)).
  • Relational GNN Support: Exports dense per-corridor adjacency ((E, N, N)) and spatial edge features ((E, N, N, 3)), plus a zero-dependency batch_graphs() converter to block-diagonal PyG COO tensors (edge_index, edge_attr, batch).
  • Auto-Reset Semantics: Finished corridors immediately reset inside the same step() call while preserving final_observation, final_state, and final_info for exact GAE bootstrapping.
  • Cross-Platform Multiprocessing: AsyncVectorScrollSwarm uses the spawn context and shards corridors across num_workers CPU processes, pairing seamlessly with backend="cpp" (zero JIT warmup).

docs.title: Quick Usage
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from scrollswarm import AsyncVectorScrollSwarm, BaseVectorScrollSwarm

# Launch 8 corridors distributed across 4 CPU workers using the C++20 kernel
with AsyncVectorScrollSwarm(
    num_envs=8,
    num_workers=4,
    num_agents=4,
    max_cycles=500,
    comm_topology="radius",
    backend="auto",
) as vec_env:
    obs, infos = vec_env.reset(seed=42)
    # obs: (8, 4, 16), infos["state"]: (8, 64), infos["alive_mask"]: (8, 4)

    for _ in range(200):
        actions = vec_env.action_space.sample()  # shape (8, 4)
        obs, rewards, terminations, truncations, infos = vec_env.step(actions)

        # Convert dense graphs to PyG-compatible block-diagonal COO batch
        edge_index, edge_attr, batch = BaseVectorScrollSwarm.batch_graphs(
            infos["adj"], infos["edge_attr"]
        )

class BaseVectorScrollSwarm(ABC):
    """
    Abstract base class for vectorized CTDE & graph-aware ScrollSwarm runners.

    Manages ``num_envs`` parallel corridors of ``num_agents`` UAVs and exposes
    batched ``(E, N, ...)`` spaces, auto-reset seeding, and block-diagonal PyG
    graph conversion utilities.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        num_envs: int,
        num_agents: int = 5,
        max_cycles: int = 1000,
        map_config: Optional[MapConfig] = None,
        comm_topology: Union[TopologyType, str] = TopologyType.CHAIN,
        target_reward: float = 1.0,
        crash_penalty: float = 10.0,
        step_reward: float = 0.01,
        team_reward: bool = False,
        backend: str = "auto",
    ):
        """
        Initializes shared spaces and environment configuration.

        Args:
            num_envs: Number of parallel corridors ``E`` (must be >= 1).
            num_agents: Number of UAVs ``N`` per corridor in ``[1, 10]``.
            max_cycles: Episode truncation horizon per corridor.
            map_config: Optional ``MapConfig`` applied to all corridors.
            comm_topology: Graph topology for inter-drone message passing.
            target_reward: Reward for photographing a target.
            crash_penalty: Penalty applied on fatal collision.
            step_reward: Per-step survival reward.
            team_reward: Whether target rewards are shared among living drones.
            backend: Geometry backend (``"auto"``, ``"numpy"``, ``"numba"``, ``"cpp"``).
        """
        if num_envs < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"num_envs must be >= 1, got {num_envs}")
        if not (1 <= num_agents <= 10):
            raise ValueError(f"num_agents must be between 1 and 10, got {num_agents}")

        self.num_envs = int(num_envs)
        self.num_agents = int(num_agents)
        self._env_kwargs: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "num_agents": self.num_agents,
            "max_cycles": max_cycles,
            "map_config": map_config,
            "comm_topology": comm_topology,
            "target_reward": target_reward,
            "crash_penalty": crash_penalty,
            "step_reward": step_reward,
            "team_reward": team_reward,
            "backend": backend,
        }
        self._closed = False
        self._episode_counter = 0
        self._base_seed: Optional[int] = None

        self.single_observation_space = spaces.Box(
            low=-1.0, high=1.0, shape=(16,), dtype=np.float32
        )
        self.single_action_space = spaces.Discrete(3)
        self.single_state_space = spaces.Box(
            low=-1.0, high=1.0, shape=(16 * self.num_agents,), dtype=np.float32
        )

        self.observation_space = spaces.Box(
            low=-1.0,
            high=1.0,
            shape=(self.num_envs, self.num_agents, 16),
            dtype=np.float32,
        )
        self.action_space = spaces.MultiDiscrete(
            np.full((self.num_envs, self.num_agents), 3, dtype=np.int64)
        )
        self.state_space = spaces.Box(
            low=-1.0,
            high=1.0,
            shape=(self.num_envs, 16 * self.num_agents),
            dtype=np.float32,
        )

    def _initial_seeds(self, seed: Optional[int]) -> List[Optional[int]]:
        """Generates distinct deterministic per-corridor seeds when ``seed`` is set."""
        self._base_seed = seed
        self._episode_counter = self.num_envs
        if seed is None:
            return [None] * self.num_envs
        return [int(seed) + e for e in range(self.num_envs)]

    def _next_autoreset_seeds(self) -> List[Optional[int]]:
        """Generates fresh deterministic seeds for any environments that auto-reset."""
        if self._base_seed is None:
            return [None] * self.num_envs
        seeds = [
            int(self._base_seed) + self._episode_counter + e
            for e in range(self.num_envs)
        ]
        self._episode_counter += self.num_envs
        return seeds

    def _validate_actions(self, actions: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Validates and normalizes an ``(E, N)`` action array."""
        arr = np.asarray(actions, dtype=np.int64)
        expected = (self.num_envs, self.num_agents)
        if arr.shape != expected:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected actions shape {expected}, got {arr.shape}")
        return arr

    @staticmethod
    def batch_graphs(
        adj: np.ndarray,
        edge_attr: np.ndarray,
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Converts dense ``(E, N, N)`` graphs into a block-diagonal PyG-ready COO batch.

        Each corridor ``e`` gets node indices offset by ``e * N``, guaranteeing
        strict inter-corridor edge isolation.

        Args:
            adj: Binary adjacency tensor of shape ``(E, N, N)``.
            edge_attr: Dense spatial feature tensor of shape ``(E, N, N, 3)``.

        Returns:
            edge_index: ``int64`` array of shape ``(2, E_total)`` with ``[src, tgt]``.
            edge_attr_flat: ``float32`` array of shape ``(E_total, 3)``.
            batch: ``int64`` graph membership vector of shape ``(E * N,)``.
        """
        num_envs, num_agents, _ = adj.shape
        env_idx, tgt_idx, src_idx = np.where(adj > 0.5)

        if env_idx.size == 0:
            edge_index = np.zeros((2, 0), dtype=np.int64)
            edge_attr_flat = np.zeros((0, 3), dtype=np.float32)
        else:
            offset = env_idx.astype(np.int64) * num_agents
            src_flat = offset + src_idx.astype(np.int64)
            tgt_flat = offset + tgt_idx.astype(np.int64)
            edge_index = np.stack([src_flat, tgt_flat], axis=0)
            edge_attr_flat = edge_attr[env_idx, tgt_idx, src_idx].astype(
                np.float32, copy=False
            )

        batch = np.repeat(np.arange(num_envs, dtype=np.int64), num_agents)
        return edge_index, edge_attr_flat, batch

    @abstractmethod
    def reset(self, seed: Optional[int] = None) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Resets all parallel corridors and returns batched observations and infos."""

    @abstractmethod
    def step(
        self, actions: np.ndarray
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Steps all parallel corridors synchronously and returns batched transitions."""

    @abstractmethod
    def close(self) -> None:
        """Releases environment or worker process resources."""

    def __enter__(self) -> "BaseVectorScrollSwarm":
        return self

    def __exit__(self, exc_type: Any, exc_val: Any, exc_tb: Any) -> None:
        self.close()

@staticmethod
def batch_graphs(
    adj: np.ndarray,
    edge_attr: np.ndarray,
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Converts dense ``(E, N, N)`` graphs into a block-diagonal PyG-ready COO batch.

    Each corridor ``e`` gets node indices offset by ``e * N``, guaranteeing
    strict inter-corridor edge isolation.

    Args:
        adj: Binary adjacency tensor of shape ``(E, N, N)``.
        edge_attr: Dense spatial feature tensor of shape ``(E, N, N, 3)``.

    Returns:
        edge_index: ``int64`` array of shape ``(2, E_total)`` with ``[src, tgt]``.
        edge_attr_flat: ``float32`` array of shape ``(E_total, 3)``.
        batch: ``int64`` graph membership vector of shape ``(E * N,)``.
    """
    num_envs, num_agents, _ = adj.shape
    env_idx, tgt_idx, src_idx = np.where(adj > 0.5)

    if env_idx.size == 0:
        edge_index = np.zeros((2, 0), dtype=np.int64)
        edge_attr_flat = np.zeros((0, 3), dtype=np.float32)
    else:
        offset = env_idx.astype(np.int64) * num_agents
        src_flat = offset + src_idx.astype(np.int64)
        tgt_flat = offset + tgt_idx.astype(np.int64)
        edge_index = np.stack([src_flat, tgt_flat], axis=0)
        edge_attr_flat = edge_attr[env_idx, tgt_idx, src_idx].astype(
            np.float32, copy=False
        )

    batch = np.repeat(np.arange(num_envs, dtype=np.int64), num_agents)
    return edge_index, edge_attr_flat, batch

class SyncVectorScrollSwarm(BaseVectorScrollSwarm):
    """
    Single-process synchronous vectorized runner for ``ScrollSwarmEnv``.

    Steps ``num_envs`` independent corridors sequentially in Python and packs
    observations, CTDE states, liveness masks, and communication graphs into
    contiguous ``(E, N, ...)`` NumPy arrays for batched neural policy inference.
    """

    def __init__(self, num_envs: int, **env_kwargs: Any):
        super().__init__(num_envs=num_envs, **env_kwargs)
        self.envs: List[ScrollSwarmEnv] = [
            ScrollSwarmEnv(**self._env_kwargs, render_mode=None)
            for _ in range(self.num_envs)
        ]
        logger.info(
            "Initialized SyncVectorScrollSwarm (num_envs=%d, num_agents=%d, backend=%s)",
            self.num_envs,
            self.num_agents,
            self._env_kwargs["backend"],
        )

    def reset(self, seed: Optional[int] = None) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:
        if self._closed:
            raise RuntimeError("Cannot reset a closed SyncVectorScrollSwarm.")
        seeds = self._initial_seeds(seed)
        results = [_reset_single_env(env, s) for env, s in zip(self.envs, seeds)]
        return _collate_reset_results(results, self.num_envs, self.num_agents)

    def step(
        self, actions: np.ndarray
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:
        if self._closed:
            raise RuntimeError("Cannot step a closed SyncVectorScrollSwarm.")
        action_arr = self._validate_actions(actions)
        autoreset_seeds = self._next_autoreset_seeds()
        results = [
            _step_and_autoreset(env, action_arr[e], autoreset_seeds[e])
            for e, env in enumerate(self.envs)
        ]
        return _collate_step_results(results, self.num_envs, self.num_agents)

    def close(self) -> None:
        if not self._closed:
            for env in self.envs:
                env.close()
            self._closed = True

class AsyncVectorScrollSwarm(BaseVectorScrollSwarm):
    """
    Multiprocess parallel vectorized runner for ``ScrollSwarmEnv``.

    Distributes ``num_envs`` independent corridors across ``num_workers`` CPU
    processes (using the cross-platform ``spawn`` context) so geometry kernels
    execute concurrently across physical CPU cores.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        num_envs: int,
        num_workers: Optional[int] = None,
        **env_kwargs: Any,
    ):
        super().__init__(num_envs=num_envs, **env_kwargs)
        cpu_count = os.cpu_count() or 1
        requested_workers = (
            min(self.num_envs, cpu_count) if num_workers is None else int(num_workers)
        )
        if requested_workers < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"num_workers must be >= 1, got {requested_workers}")
        self.num_workers = min(self.num_envs, requested_workers)

        # Partition num_envs evenly across num_workers
        base, rem = divmod(self.num_envs, self.num_workers)
        self._worker_slices: List[slice] = []
        cursor = 0
        for w in range(self.num_workers):
            count = base + (1 if w < rem else 0)
            self._worker_slices.append(slice(cursor, cursor + count))
            cursor += count

        ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
        self._parent_conns: List[Any] = []
        self._workers: List[Any] = []
        for sl in self._worker_slices:
            parent_conn, child_conn = ctx.Pipe()
            proc = ctx.Process(
                target=_worker_loop,
                args=(child_conn, sl.stop - sl.start, self._env_kwargs),
                daemon=True,
            )
            proc.start()
            child_conn.close()
            self._parent_conns.append(parent_conn)
            self._workers.append(proc)

        logger.info(
            "Initialized AsyncVectorScrollSwarm (num_envs=%d, num_workers=%d, num_agents=%d, backend=%s)",
            self.num_envs,
            self.num_workers,
            self.num_agents,
            self._env_kwargs["backend"],
        )

    def _gather_worker_results(self) -> List[Tuple[Any, ...]]:
        """Collects and flattens ordered results from all worker pipes."""
        merged: List[Tuple[Any, ...]] = []
        for conn in self._parent_conns:
            status, payload = conn.recv()
            if status == "error":
                raise RuntimeError(f"AsyncVectorScrollSwarm worker failed: {payload}")
            merged.extend(payload)
        return merged

    def reset(self, seed: Optional[int] = None) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:
        if self._closed:
            raise RuntimeError("Cannot reset a closed AsyncVectorScrollSwarm.")
        seeds = self._initial_seeds(seed)
        for conn, sl in zip(self._parent_conns, self._worker_slices):
            conn.send(("reset", seeds[sl]))
        results = self._gather_worker_results()
        return _collate_reset_results(results, self.num_envs, self.num_agents)

    def step(
        self, actions: np.ndarray
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:
        if self._closed:
            raise RuntimeError("Cannot step a closed AsyncVectorScrollSwarm.")
        action_arr = self._validate_actions(actions)
        autoreset_seeds = self._next_autoreset_seeds()
        for conn, sl in zip(self._parent_conns, self._worker_slices):
            conn.send(("step", (action_arr[sl], autoreset_seeds[sl])))
        results = self._gather_worker_results()
        return _collate_step_results(results, self.num_envs, self.num_agents)

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self._closed:
            return
        self._closed = True
        for conn in self._parent_conns:
            try:
                conn.send(("close", None))
            except (BrokenPipeError, EOFError, OSError):
                pass
        for proc in self._workers:
            proc.join(timeout=2.0)
            if proc.is_alive():
                proc.terminate()
                proc.join(timeout=1.0)
        for conn in self._parent_conns:
            try:
                conn.close()
            except OSError:
                pass

    def __del__(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.close()
        except Exception:
            pass

docs.title: Action Space & Kinematics
docs.text: Each drone moves only along the vertical axis using three discrete actions. This page defines the action space, altitude update rules, crash handling, and joint action scaling.

docs.title: 1. Discrete Action Space
docs.text:
Each autonomous UAV \(i \in \{1, \dots, N\}\) operates over a discrete action space conforming to Gymnasium and PettingZoo standards:

\[\mathcal{A}_i = \{0, 1, 2\} \equiv \{\text{UP}, \;\text{STAY}, \;\text{DOWN}\} \quad \big(\mathcal{A}_i \cong \text{Discrete}(3)\big)\] Action Index Identifier Vertical Velocity / Thrust Physical Displacement \(\Delta y\) Description 0 Action.UP Negative vertical velocity \(\Delta y = -k\text{ px}\) Ascends (climbs) toward higher altitude 1 Action.STAY Zero vertical velocity \(\Delta y = 0\text{ px}\) Maintains current flight altitude 2 Action.DOWN Positive vertical velocity \(\Delta y = +k\text{ px}\) Descends (dives) toward lower altitude

By default, the vertical step size is \(k = 5\text{ px/step}\).

docs.title: 2.1 State Evolution
docs.text:
At time step \(t\), UAV \(i\) is positioned at \((x_i, y_i(t))\). Because UAVs occupy fixed longitudinal station-keeping columns along the \(x\)-axis, horizontal coordinates remain fixed in the screen frame:

\[x_i(t+1) = x_i(t)\]

Vertical altitude evolves according to the selected discrete action \(a_{i, t} \in \mathcal{A}_i\):

\[y_{i, t+1} = \text{clip}\left( y_{i, t} + \Delta y(a_{i, t}), \quad \frac{h_{\text{uav}}}{2}, \quad H - \frac{h_{\text{uav}}}{2} \right)\]

Where:

  • \(h_{\text{uav}} = 16.0\text{ px}\) is the physical bounding height of the UAV.
  • \(H = 400\text{ px}\) is the total corridor height.
  • Clamping ensures the drone geometry physically remains within the screen bounds even before boundary collision checks occur.

docs.title: 2.2 Crashed UAV Invariant
docs.text:
If a UAV collides with an obstacle or corridor boundary at time \(t\), it crashes (alive = False):

\[\text{If } \text{alive}_i(t) = \text{False} \implies y_{i, t+1} = y_{i, t}, \quad \text{no actions executed}\]

Crashed drones become inactive obstacles on the field; their actions are ignored, and they are pruned from env.agents.

docs.title: 3. Joint Action Space
docs.text:
In multi-agent systems with \(N\) drones, the joint action space \(\pmb{\mathcal{A}}\) is the Cartesian product of the individual action spaces (Boutilier, 1996; Oliehoek & Amato, 2016):

\[\pmb{\mathcal{A}} = \mathcal{A}_1 \times \mathcal{A}_2 \times \dots \times \mathcal{A}_N = \{0, 1, 2\}^N\]

The cardinality of the joint action space grows exponentially with swarm size \(N\):

\[|\pmb{\mathcal{A}}| = 3^N\] Swarm Size \(N\) Joint Action Combinations \(\|\pmb{\mathcal{A}}\|\) Complexity Class 1 \(3^1 = 3\) Standard single-agent discrete space 3 \(3^3 = 27\) Easily solvable via centralized value iteration 5 (Default) \(3^5 = 243\) Combinatorial multi-agent coordination 8 \(3^8 = 6,561\) Requires factorized value functions (e.g., QMIX, VDN) 10 (Maximum) \(3^{10} = 59,049\) High-dimensional joint action space

This combinatorial growth illustrates why independent decentralized execution or factorized value decomposition is necessary for large swarms.

docs.text:
1. Boutilier, C. (1996). Planning, learning and coordination in multiagent decision processes. In Proceedings of the 6th Conference on Theoretical Aspects of Rationality and Knowledge (TARK), pp. 195–210. ACM DL: 237197.
  2. Sutton, R. S., & Barto, A. G. (2018). Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (2nd Edition). MIT Press. Book Link.

docs.title: Communication Graph & Network Topologies
docs.text: Decentralized drones use a dynamic communication graph to coordinate beyond their local field of view. This page defines the five supported graph topologies, how links are pruned when drones crash, and the message aggregation operators.

docs.title: 1. Graph Communication Model
docs.text:
In multi-agent reinforcement learning, decentralized agents often need to coordinate beyond their local field of view by sharing intermediate representations or messages (Sukhbaatar et al., 2016; Das et al., 2019).

In ScrollSwarm, the communication network at time \(t\) is represented as a directed graph:

\[\mathcal{G}(t) = \big( \mathcal{V}(t), \;\mathcal{E}(t) \big)\]

Where:

  • \(\mathcal{V}(t) \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}\) is the active node set consisting of all living UAVs:
\[\mathcal{V}(t) = \big\{ i \in \{1, \dots, N\} \;\big|\; \text{alive}_i(t) = \text{True} \big\}\]
  • \(\mathcal{E}(t) \subseteq \mathcal{V}(t) \times \mathcal{V}(t)\) is the directed edge set, where \((j, i) \in \mathcal{E}(t)\) denotes an active communication channel from source UAV \(j\) to target UAV \(i\).
  • \(\mathbf{A}(t) \in \{0, 1\}^{N \times N}\) is the binary adjacency matrix where \(A_{ij}(t) = 1 \iff (j, i) \in \mathcal{E}(t)\).

docs.title: 2. Supported Topologies
docs.text: ScrollSwarm provides five canonical graph communication topologies:

docs.title: 2.1 Chain Topology
docs.text:
Models a sequential line-of-sight daisy-chain along horizontal station-keeping columns:

\[A_{ij} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } |i - j| = 1 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\]
  • Each internal UAV communicates exclusively with its immediate left and right neighbors (\(i-1\) and \(i+1\)).
  • Maximum node degree: \(\Delta = 2\).

docs.title: 2.2 Ring Topology
docs.text:
A 1D periodic cycle graph connecting adjacent neighbors with wrap-around between the first and last drones:

\[A_{ij} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } (i - j) \equiv \pm 1 \pmod N \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\]
  • Eliminates boundary edge effects present in open chains.
  • Every node has degree precisely 2 (2-regular graph).

docs.title: 2.3 Full Broadcast Topology
docs.text:
A complete directed graph representing global, unconstrained broadcast communication (all-to-all):

\[A_{ij} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } i \neq j \\ 0 & \text{if } i = j \end{cases}\]
  • Number of edges: \(E = N(N - 1)\).
  • Serves as the theoretical upper bound for collaborative information exchange.

docs.title: 2.4 Spatial Radius Disk Graph
docs.text:
A geometric random graph where a communication link exists if and only if the Euclidean distance between two drones is within communication radius \(R_{\text{comm}}\):

\[A_{ij} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } 0 < \|\mathbf{p}_i - \mathbf{p}_j\| \le R_{\text{comm}} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\]

By default, \(R_{\text{comm}} = 180.0\text{ px}\). Links dynamically form and break as drones climb and dive.

docs.title: 2.5 Degree-Capped Spatial Graph
docs.text:
Connects each UAV to its \(k\)-nearest spatial neighbors, enforcing a strict bandwidth/degree cap (\(k = \text{max_degree}\), default: \(2\)):

\[\mathcal{N}_k(i) = \arg\min_{\mathcal{S} \subseteq \mathcal{V} \setminus \{i\}, |\mathcal{S}| \le k} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{S}} \|\mathbf{p}_i - \mathbf{p}_j\|\] \[A_{ij} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } j \in \mathcal{N}_k(i) \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\]

docs.title: 3. Dynamic Dead-Agent Edge Pruning Invariant
docs.text:
In real-world swarm robotics, crashed agents cannot transmit or receive radio messages. ScrollSwarm enforces strict dynamic edge pruning (Oliehoek & Amato, 2016):

For all pairs \((i, j) \in \{1, \dots, N\}^2\) and all time steps \(t\):

\[A_{ij}(t) = A_{ij}^{\text{base}} \cdot \mathbf{1}_{\text{alive}_i(t)} \cdot \mathbf{1}_{\text{alive}_j(t)}\]

If drone \(k\) crashes (\(\text{alive}_k = \text{False}\)), row \(k\) and column \(k\) of \(\mathbf{A}(t)\) are zeroed immediately:

\[\sum_{j=1}^N A_{kj}(t) = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \sum_{i=1}^N A_{ik}(t) = 0\]

All incident edges vanish from the graph, preventing stale messages from reaching Graph Neural Networks.

docs.title: 4. Message Passing & Permutation-Invariant Aggregation
docs.text: In cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning with networked communication (Sukhbaatar et al., 2016; Das et al., 2019; Jiang et al., 2020), decentralized UAVs coordinate by exchanging messages over the active communication graph \(\mathcal{G}(t) = (\mathcal{V}(t), \mathcal{E}(t))\).

docs.title: 4.1 Two-Stage Communication & Decision Epoch
docs.text:
Under the Dec-POMDP-Comm formulation, each decision step proceeds in two distinct phases:

  1. Message Generation: Each active agent \(j \in \mathcal{V}(t)\) produces a message vector \(\mathbf{m}_j \in \mathbb{R}^M\) conditioned on its private observation or latent state encoding: $\(\mathbf{m}_j = f_{\text{enc}}(o_j)\)$
  2. Channel Broadcast: Agent \(j\) transmits message \(\mathbf{m}_j\) along all outgoing directed links \((j, i) \in \mathcal{E}(t)\).
  3. Neighborhood Aggregation: Receiving agent \(i\) aggregates all messages arriving from its in-neighborhood \(\mathcal{N}_{\text{in}}(i) = \{j \in \mathcal{V}(t) \mid (j, i) \in \mathcal{E}(t)\}\) using a permutation-invariant aggregation operator \(\bigoplus\): $\(\tilde{\mathbf{m}}_i = \bigoplus_{j \in \mathcal{N}_{\text{in}}(i)} \mathbf{m}_j\)$ (If \(|\mathcal{N}_{\text{in}}(i)| = 0\), the incoming message context defaults to \(\tilde{\mathbf{m}}_i = \mathbf{0}_M\)).
  4. Action Selection: The decentralized policy of agent \(i\) conditions jointly on its private observation \(o_i\) and the received neighborhood context \(\tilde{\mathbf{m}}_i\): $\(a_i \sim \pi_i(a_i \mid o_i, \tilde{\mathbf{m}}_i)\)$

docs.title: 4.2 Permutation-Invariant Aggregation Operators
docs.text:
Because in-degrees vary dynamically across topologies (e.g., spatial radius disks and dead-agent edge pruning), the aggregation function \(\bigoplus\) must produce the same output regardless of neighbor ordering:

\[\bigoplus \big( \mathbf{m}_{\sigma(1)}, \dots, \mathbf{m}_{\sigma(k)} \big) = \bigoplus \big( \mathbf{m}_1, \dots, \mathbf{m}_k \big) \quad \forall \sigma \in \mathcal{S}_k\]

ScrollSwarm formalizes four canonical aggregation operators:

Operator Mathematical Formulation Properties & Theoretical Role Mean (\(\text{mean}\)) \(\tilde{\mathbf{m}}_i = \frac{1}{\|\mathcal{N}_{\text{in}}(i)\|} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{N}_{\text{in}}(i)} \mathbf{m}_j\) Degree-normalized representation; prevents signal magnitude explosion as swarm density scales (CommNet). Sum (\(\text{sum}\)) \(\tilde{\mathbf{m}}_i = \sum_{j \in \mathcal{N}_{\text{in}}(i)} \mathbf{m}_j\) Cardinality-sensitive; preserves additive count information (e.g., how many teammates detect a target). Max (\(\text{max}\)) \(\tilde{\mathbf{m}}_i = \max_{j \in \mathcal{N}_{\text{in}}(i)} \mathbf{m}_j\) Element-wise max-pooling; filters for peak salient alert signals across the neighborhood. Ordered Concatenation (\(\text{concat}\)) \(\tilde{\mathbf{m}}_i = \big[ \mathbf{m}_{j_1}^\top, \dots, \mathbf{m}_{j_k}^\top \big]^\top\) Fixed-degree ordered concatenation; preserves directional identity for regular topologies (Ring, Chain).

Note on Concrete Tensors

For PyTorch Geometric tensor formats (edge_index, edge_attr) and runtime routing code, see the Configuration & Technical Reference.

docs.title: Environment Dynamics
docs.text: This page defines the 2D corridor geometry, scrolling kinematics, procedural obstacles, guaranteed navigable gap proof, and collision checks.

docs.title: 1. Coordinate Frame & World Geometry
docs.text:
ScrollSwarm is modeled in a 2D Cartesian coordinate system:

  • Horizontal Axis (\(x\)): Represents forward distance along the flight path (in pixels/meters). Space flows from right to left as the environment scrolls.
  • Vertical Axis (\(y\)): Represents flight altitude, measured downwards from the screen ceiling (\(y = 0\)) to the ground floor (\(y = H\)).
\[\mathcal{W} = \big\{ (x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 \;\big|\; 0 \le x \le W, \quad y_{\text{ceil}} \le y \le y_{\text{floor}} \big\}\]

Where:

  • \(W\): Corridor width (default: \(800\text{ px}\)).
  • \(H\): Corridor total height (default: \(400\text{ px}\)).
  • \(y_{\text{ceil}}\): High-altitude boundary ceiling (\(y_{\text{ceil}} = 15\text{ px}\)).
  • \(y_{\text{floor}}\): Ground surface boundary (\(y_{\text{floor}} = H - 15 = 385\text{ px}\)).

docs.title: 2. World Kinematics & Scrolling Evolution
docs.text: The simulation advances in discrete time steps \(\Delta t\) at a nominal rate of \(30\text{ FPS}\).

docs.title: 2.1 Forward Scrolling Motion
docs.text:
The corridor scrolls horizontally leftward at constant velocity \(v_{\text{scroll}}\):

\[x_{t+1} = x_t - v_{\text{scroll}} \cdot \Delta t\]

By default, \(v_{\text{scroll}} = 1.0\text{ px/step}\). Because all drones occupy stationary horizontal observation columns on the left portion of the screen (\(x \in [80, 320]\)), the relative approach velocity of obstacles and targets toward the swarm is precisely \(v_{\text{scroll}}\).

docs.title: 2.2 Procedural Obstacle Models
docs.text:
Obstacles represent physical hazards of varying geometries and scales:

  1. Ground-Standing Structures:

    • Modeled as axis-aligned rectangles rooted at the ground plane \(y_{\text{floor}}\): \(\text{Rect}_{\text{ground}} = \big[ x - w/2, \;x + w/2 \big] \times \big[ y_{\text{floor}} - h, \;y_{\text{floor}} \big]\)
    • Width \(w \sim \mathcal{U}(30.0, 70.0)\text{ px}\).
    • Height \(h \sim \mathcal{U}(40.0, h_{\max})\text{ px}\).

  2. Overhead Structures:

    • Modeled as rectangular barriers hanging down from the ceiling \(y_{\text{ceil}}\): \(\text{Rect}_{\text{overhead}} = \big[ x - w/2, \;x + w/2 \big] \times \big[ y_{\text{ceil}}, \;y_{\text{ceil}} + d \big]\)
    • Width \(w \sim \mathcal{U}(30.0, 70.0)\text{ px}\).
    • Depth \(d \sim \mathcal{U}(30.0, d_{\max})\text{ px}\).

  3. Floating Debris & Airborne Hazards: Modeled as convex polygons with radius \(r \sim \mathcal{U}(14.0, 32.0)\text{ px}\) undergoing epicyclic vertical oscillation: \(y(t) = y_{\text{base}} + A \sin(\omega t + \phi)\), where amplitude \(A \sim \mathcal{U}(4.0, 16.0)\text{ px}\), frequency \(\omega \sim \mathcal{U}(0.02, 0.06)\text{ rad/step}\), and initial phase \(\phi \sim \mathcal{U}(0, 2\pi)\).

docs.title: 3. Guaranteed Navigable Passage Invariant
docs.text: A critical benchmark design requirement in autonomous navigation is that an environment must never generate provably impassable bottlenecks (Siegwart et al., 2011; LaValle, 2006).

docs.title: 3.1 Theorem: Passage Solvability Invariant
docs.text:
Let \(G(x, t)\) denote the vertical gap between the lowest point of any overhead obstacle and the highest point of any ground obstacle at horizontal coordinate \(x\):

\[G(x, t) = y_{\text{ground_top}}(x, t) - y_{\text{overhead_bottom}}(x, t)\]

Invariant: For all horizontal positions \(x \in [0, W]\) and all time steps \(t \ge 0\):

\[G(x, t) \ge G_{\min} = 110\text{ px}\]

Proof: When an overhead structure with depth \(d\) and a ground structure with height \(h\) coexist at coordinate \(x\):

  1. The available vertical height between baseline boundaries is \(\Delta Y = y_{\text{floor}} - y_{\text{ceil}} = 385 - 15 = 370\text{ px}\).
  2. In _create_procedural_obstacle(), the maximum allowable structure dimension is bounded by: \(h_{\max} = d_{\max} = \Delta Y - G_{\min} - 10 = 370 - 110 - 10 = 250\text{ px}\)
  3. Spawning intervals strictly enforce alternating placement or vertical margin checks. Therefore: \(G(x, t) = \Delta Y - (h + d) \ge 370 - 250 = 120\text{ px} > 110\text{ px}\)

Hence, the corridor unconditionally satisfies \(G(x, t) \ge 110\text{ px}\), guaranteeing sufficient clearance for UAV quadcopters (collision height \(16\text{ px}\)).

docs.title: 4. Analytical Collision Detection
docs.text:
Physical collision between a drone and an obstacle is computed using exact point-to-polygon Euclidean distance and ray-casting containment tests:

  1. Bounding Circle Rejection: If \(\sqrt{(x_{\text{uav}} - x_{\text{obs}})^2 + (y_{\text{uav}} - y_{\text{obs}})^2} > R_{\text{uav}} + R_{\text{obs}}\), no collision is possible.
  2. Ray-Casting Inside-Polygon Test: A horizontal ray is cast from \((x_{\text{uav}}, y_{\text{uav}})\) to \(+\infty\). If the ray intersects an odd number of polygon boundary edges, the drone is inside the obstacle (Jordan Curve Theorem).
  3. Point-to-Segment Edge Distance: For each polygon edge segment \(\mathbf{e} = (\mathbf{v}_a, \mathbf{v}_b)\), the minimum distance to \((x_{\text{uav}}, y_{\text{uav}})\) is computed analytically via vector projection:
\[\mathbf{p}_{\text{proj}} = \mathbf{v}_a + \text{clip}\left(\frac{(\mathbf{p} - \mathbf{v}_a) \cdot (\mathbf{v}_b - \mathbf{v}_a)}{\|\mathbf{v}_b - \mathbf{v}_a\|^2}, \;0, \;1\right) (\mathbf{v}_b - \mathbf{v}_a)\]

If \(\min_e \|\mathbf{p} - \mathbf{p}_{\text{proj}}\| \le R_{\text{uav}}\), a collision occurs.

docs.title: Observation Space
docs.text: Each drone acts on local sensor readings while centralized critics can read the full team state during training. This page defines the 7-ray forward LiDAR, the probabilistic camera model, the 16-dimensional observation vector, and the centralized CTDE state representation.

docs.title: 1. Sensory Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Each UAV in ScrollSwarm operates under partial observability, constructing a local 16-dimensional observation vector \(\mathbf{o}_i \in [-1.0, 1.0]^{16}\) from four components:

  1. Normalized Altitude State (\(1\) float): Normalized vertical flight coordinate \(y_i / H \in [0.0, 1.0]\).
  2. Forward 7-Ray LiDAR (\(7\) floats): Rangefinder beam array measuring normalized intersection distances to approaching obstacles and corridor boundaries (\(d_k^* / R_{\max} \in [0.0, 1.0]\)).
  3. Target Tracking Vector (\(4\) floats): Relative horizontal displacement, vertical displacement, Euclidean distance, and photo inspection range indicator to the nearest unphotographed target.
  4. Neighbor Drone Vector (\(4\) floats): Relative horizontal displacement, vertical displacement, Euclidean distance, and communication connectivity indicator to the nearest living teammate.

docs.title: 2.1 Theoretical Foundation: The Beam Model of Range Finders
docs.text:
Range sensing in ScrollSwarm builds on the Beam Model of Range Finders (Thrun, Burgard, & Fox, 2005, Chapter 6):

\[p(z \mid x, m) = \prod_{k=1}^K p(z_k \mid x, m)\]

Where an array of \(K = 7\) range rays is projected from the UAV position \((x_i, y_i)\) into the oncoming corridor airspace.

docs.title: 2.2 Beam Geometry & Field of View
docs.text:
The 7 sensor beams span a forward field of view \(\text{FOV} = 120^\circ\) centered horizontally forward along the direction of flight:

\[\theta_k = -\frac{\pi}{3} + k \cdot \frac{2\pi}{3(K - 1)}, \quad k \in \{0, 1, \dots, 6\}\] \[\Theta = \big\{ -60^\circ, \;-40^\circ, \;-20^\circ, \;0^\circ, \;+20^\circ, \;+40^\circ, \;+60^\circ \big\}\]
  • Maximum Range: \(R_{\max} = 400.0\text{ px}\) (spanning the oncoming half of the \(800\text{ px}\) corridor).
  • Beam Angle \(\theta = 0^\circ\): Projects horizontally forward to detect upcoming obstacles.
  • Beam Angles \(\theta < 0\): Point upward-forward to detect ceiling boundaries and overhead structures.
  • Beam Angles \(\theta > 0\): Point downward-forward to detect ground structures and terrain boundaries.

                  Ray 1 (-40°)   \
                  Ray 2 (-20°)    \
  UAV [x, y] ---------------------- Ray 3 (0°, Forward)
                  Ray 4 (+20°)    /
                  Ray 5 (+40°)   /
                  Ray 6 (+60°)  /

docs.title: 2.3 Ray-Casting & Determinant Intersection Math
docs.text:
For each beam \(k\) with unit direction vector \(\mathbf{u}_k = (\cos \theta_k, \sin \theta_k)\), the true range \(d_k^*\) is computed as the minimum intersection distance across all environmental primitives:

\[d_k^* = \min \big( R_{\max}, \;t_{\text{ceil}}, \;t_{\text{floor}}, \;\min_{j} t_{\text{obs}, j} \big)\]

  1. Analytical Boundary Intersections:

    If \(\sin \theta_k < 0\), then:

    \[t_{\text{ceil}} = \frac{y_{\text{ceil}} - y_i}{\sin \theta_k}\]

    If \(\sin \theta_k > 0\), then:

    \[t_{\text{floor}} = \frac{y_{\text{floor}} - y_i}{\sin \theta_k}\]

  2. Ray-Segment Determinant Intersection for Polygon Edges:

    For a polygon edge with endpoints \(\mathbf{v}_a = (x_a, y_a)\) and \(\mathbf{v}_b = (x_b, y_b)\), the parametric ray \(\mathbf{p}(t) = \mathbf{p}_0 + t \mathbf{u}_k\) and edge segment \(\mathbf{e}(u) = \mathbf{v}_a + u(\mathbf{v}_b - \mathbf{v}_a)\) intersect when:

    $\(t = \frac{(x_a - x_i)(y_b - y_a) - (y_a - y_i)(x_b - x_a)}{\cos \theta_k (y_b - y_a) - \sin \theta_k (x_b - x_a)}\)$

    and

    $\(u = \frac{(x_a - x_i)\sin \theta_k - (y_a - y_i)\cos \theta_k}{\cos \theta_k (y_b - y_a) - \sin \theta_k (x_b - x_a)}\)$

An intersection is valid if \(0 \le t < R_{\max}\) and \(0 \le u \le 1\).

  1. Normalization:

    $\(d_{\text{norm}, k} = \frac{d_k^*}{R_{\max}} \in [0.0, 1.0]\)$

docs.title: 3.1 Proximity-Dependent Bernoulli Detection
docs.text:
Target observation is modeled as a stochastic inspection process under camera sensor uncertainty, following standard mobile sensor network models (Cortés et al., 2004; Beard & McLain, 2012).

A target located at \((x_{\text{tgt}}, y_{\text{tgt}})\) can only be photographed if a drone \(j\) is within the physical inspection radius:

\[d_j = \sqrt{(x_j - x_{\text{tgt}})^2 + (y_j - y_{\text{tgt}})^2} \le D_{\text{photo}} = 45.0\text{ px}\]

The probability of drone \(j\) capturing a clear, high-quality photograph is a function of proximity and intrinsic sensor reliability:

\[P_j(\text{clear} \mid d_j) = \left( 1 - \frac{d_j}{D_{\text{photo}}} \right) \cdot \mu_{\text{sensor}}\]

Where:

  • \(D_{\text{photo}} = 45.0\text{ px}\) is the maximum photo radius.
  • \(\mu_{\text{sensor}} = 0.85\) models camera blur, lighting variations, and vibration disturbances.

docs.title: 3.2 Swarm Team Redundancy
docs.text:
When multiple living drones \(\mathcal{N}_{\text{target}}\) are simultaneously within photo range of the target, their observations are conditionally independent Bernoulli trials:

\[P_{\text{team}}(\text{success}) = 1 - \prod_{j \in \mathcal{N}_{\text{target}}} \Big( 1 - P_j(\text{clear} \mid d_j) \Big)\]

If \(X \sim \text{Bernoulli}(P_{\text{team}})\) yields \(1\), the target is successfully photographed, marked completed, and awards the team inspection reward. This mathematical formulation naturally incentivizes multi-UAV team redundancy: if one drone is near the perimeter (\(P_1 = 0.2\)), a second drone flying close (\(P_2 = 0.8\)) elevates the team capture probability to:

\[P_{\text{team}} = 1 - (1 - 0.2)(1 - 0.8) = 1 - (0.8 \times 0.2) = 0.84\]

(Defaults: LiDAR indices 1–7 return \(1.0\) when no obstacle is within \(R_{\max}\); target indices 8–11 default to \([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0]\) when no active targets exist; neighbor indices 12–15 default to \([0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0]\) when no living neighbors exist.)

docs.title: 5. Centralized State Space for CTDE
docs.text:
For algorithms employing Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (such as MAPPO, QMIX, and MADDPG), env.state() returns the global concatenated state vector:

\[\mathbf{s} = \big[ \mathbf{o}_1^\top, \;\mathbf{o}_2^\top, \;\dots, \;\mathbf{o}_N^\top \big]^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{16N}\]
  • State Space: spaces.Box(low=-1.0, high=1.0, shape=(16 * num_agents,), dtype=np.float32).
  • Dead Agent Zero-Masking: If agent \(i\) has crashed (alive = False), its corresponding slice in the state vector is replaced with zero: \(\mathbf{o}_i = \mathbf{0}_{16} \quad \text{if } \text{alive}_i = \text{False}\).

docs.title: Decision-Theoretic Formulations
docs.text: ScrollSwarm is a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) benchmark that supports multiple formal decision-theoretic frameworks depending on team size, observability, and communication settings.

docs.title: 1. Decision-Theoretic Framework Taxonomy
docs.text:
The following matrix summarizes the fundamental decision-theoretic models formalized in the reinforcement learning literature (Puterman, 1994; Kaelbling et al., 1998; Oliehoek & Amato, 2016). All listed models are natively supported by ScrollSwarm:

Model Scale Observability Communication MDP Single Full None POMDP Single Partial None MMDP Multi Full None Dec-MDP Multi Jointly Full None Dec-POMDP Multi Partial None Dec-POMDP-Comm Multi Partial Integrated (Graph \(\mathcal{G}\))

ScrollSwarm Support

By configuring swarm size (num_agents=1 vs. \(N \ge 2\)), enabling or bypassing graph communication (comm_topology), and selecting decentralized observations vs. centralized state vectors (env.state()), ScrollSwarm seamlessly maps to any of these six formulations.

docs.title: 2.1 Markov Decision Process (MDP)
docs.text:
When ScrollSwarm is configured with a single UAV (\(N=1\)) having access to the complete environment state, the problem reduces to a classical MDP (Bellman, 1957; Puterman, 1994):

\[\mathcal{M}_{\text{MDP}} = \langle \mathcal{S}, \mathcal{A}, \mathcal{T}, \mathcal{R}, \gamma \rangle\]
  • \(\mathcal{S}\): The set of all global environmental states, including UAV coordinates \((x, y)\), active obstacle coordinates and geometry, and target states.
  • \(\mathcal{A}\): The discrete vertical action set \(\mathcal{A} = \{0: \text{UP}, 1: \text{STAY}, 2: \text{DOWN}\}\).
  • \(\mathcal{T}(s' \mid s, a)\): State transition probability function \(P(s_{t+1} = s' \mid s_t = s, a_t = a)\), deterministic for kinematics and stochastic for target spawning.
  • \(\mathcal{R}(s, a)\): Real-valued scalar reward function evaluating step survival, obstacle collision, and target photography.
  • \(\gamma \in [0, 1)\): The discount factor for future returns.

docs.title: 2.2 Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP)
docs.text:
In realistic single-UAV operations, the agent cannot perceive the global state \(\mathcal{S}\) directly; it must act based on its local, bounded sensor readings (Kaelbling, Littman, & Cassandra, 1998; Kochenderfer et al., 2015):

\[\mathcal{M}_{\text{POMDP}} = \langle \mathcal{S}, \mathcal{A}, \mathcal{T}, \mathcal{R}, \Omega, \mathcal{O}, \gamma \rangle\]
  • \(\Omega\): The observation space, represented by the 16-dimensional continuous feature vector \(\mathbf{o} \in [-1.0, 1.0]^{16}\).
  • \(\mathcal{O}(o \mid s', a)\): The observation emission probability distribution \(P(o_{t+1} = o \mid s_{t+1} = s', a_t = a)\), capturing forward 7-ray LiDAR rangefinder intersections and bearing measurements.

docs.title: 2.3 Multi-Agent MDP (MMDP)
docs.text:
When \(N\) cooperative UAVs share full state information and are controlled by a centralized decision-maker (Boutilier, 1996):

\[\mathcal{M}_{\text{MMDP}} = \langle \mathcal{I}, \mathcal{S}, \{\mathcal{A}_i\}, \mathcal{T}, \mathcal{R}, \gamma \rangle\]
  • \(\mathcal{I} = \{1, \dots, N\}\): The finite set of \(N\) UAV agents.
  • \(\mathcal{A} = \prod_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \mathcal{A}_i\): The joint action space of size \(|\mathcal{A}| = 3^N\).
  • \(\mathcal{R}(s, \mathbf{a})\): Shared global team reward evaluating the collective performance of all UAVs.

docs.title: 2.4 Decentralized POMDP (Dec-POMDP)
docs.text:
When \(N\) agents must choose actions independently based solely on their individual, local action-observation histories without communication (Bernstein et al., 2002; Oliehoek & Amato, 2016):

\[\mathcal{M}_{\text{Dec-POMDP}} = \langle \mathcal{I}, \mathcal{S}, \{\mathcal{A}_i\}, \mathcal{T}, \mathcal{R}, \{\Omega_i\}, \mathcal{O}, \gamma \rangle\]
  • \(\Omega_i\): The local observation space of agent \(i\) (\(\mathbb{R}^{16}\)).
  • \(\mathcal{O}(o_1, \dots, o_N \mid s', \mathbf{a})\): The joint observation emission probability function \(P(\mathbf{o} \mid s', \mathbf{a})\).
  • Each agent \(i\) executes a decentralized policy \(\pi_i(a_i \mid \tau_i)\), where \(\tau_i = (o_i^0, a_i^0, \dots, o_i^t) \in (\Omega_i \times \mathcal{A}_i)^* \times \Omega_i\) is the agent's private history.
  • The collective objective is to find a joint policy \(\pi^* = \langle \pi_1^*, \dots, \pi_N^* \rangle\) that maximizes expected discounted cumulative team return: $\(J(\pi) = \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \gamma^t \mathcal{R}(s_t, \mathbf{a}_t) \;\Bigg|\; \mathbf{a}_t \sim \pi(\cdot \mid \pmb{\tau}_t) \right]\)$

docs.title: 2.5 Decentralized POMDP with Communication (Dec-POMDP-Comm)
docs.text:
The canonical formulation of ScrollSwarm incorporates explicit inter-agent communication channels over a dynamic network graph \(\mathcal{G} = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E})\) (Xuan, Lesser, & Zilberstein, 2001; Goldman & Zilberstein, 2004; Oliehoek & Amato, 2016):

\[\mathcal{M}_{\text{Dec-POMDP-Comm}} = \langle \mathcal{I}, \mathcal{S}, \{\mathcal{A}_i\}, \mathcal{T}, \mathcal{R}, \{\Omega_i\}, \mathcal{O}, \Sigma, \mathcal{C}, \mathcal{G}, \gamma \rangle\]
  • \(\Sigma\): The communication message alphabet (or continuous latent vector space \(\mathbb{R}^M\)).
  • \(\mathcal{C}\): Optional communication cost function (in ScrollSwarm, \(\mathcal{C} = 0\), modeling free localized broadcast).
  • \(\mathcal{G} = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E})\): Dynamic communication topology (Chain, Ring, Radius, Capped, Full) determining allowed communication links between living agents.

In each decision epoch, agents execute a two-stage step:

  1. Communication Phase: Every agent \(i\) broadcasts message \(m_i \in \Sigma\) to its graph neighbors \(\mathcal{N}(i)\).
  2. Action Phase: Agent \(i\) receives aggregated neighbor messages \(\tilde{m}_i = \bigoplus_{j \in \mathcal{N}(i)} m_j\) and selects physical action \(a_i \sim \pi_i(a_i \mid \tau_i, \tilde{m}_i)\).

docs.title: 3. Joint Observability & The Dec-MDP Property
docs.text:
A critical question in multi-agent reinforcement learning is whether the collection of local observations across all agents is sufficient to reconstruct the full underlying state of the environment.

According to Oliehoek & Amato (2016, Definition 2.4), a Dec-POMDP is jointly fully observable (and thus constitutes a Dec-MDP) if the joint observation vector \(\mathbf{o} = \langle o_1, \dots, o_N \rangle\) uniquely determines the global state:

\[\forall \mathbf{o} \in \Omega_1 \times \dots \times \Omega_N, \quad \exists s \in \mathcal{S} \quad \text{such that} \quad P(s \mid \mathbf{o}) = 1\]

In ScrollSwarm, the global state vector provided by env.state() concatenates individual observations:

\[\mathbf{s} = \big[ \mathbf{o}_1^\top, \;\mathbf{o}_2^\top, \;\dots, \;\mathbf{o}_N^\top \big]^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{16\times N}\]

This property directly enables Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) frameworks such as MAPPO (Yu et al., 2022), QMIX (Rashid et al., 2018), and MADDPG (Lowe et al., 2017), where a centralized value function \(V(s)\) or centralized action-value critic \(Q_{\text{tot}}(s, \mathbf{a})\) conditions on the joint observation during offline training, while decentralized actors \(\pi_i(a_i \mid o_i)\) operate strictly on local observations during execution.

docs.title: Rewards & Episode Horizon
docs.text: This page defines the per-step reward components, discounted return objective, and episode termination versus truncation rules.

docs.title: 1. Reward Function Formulation
docs.text:
At each simulation step \(t\), every living UAV \(i \in \mathcal{I}\) receives a scalar feedback reward \(R_i(t) \in \mathbb{R}\). The reward signal balances survival, collision avoidance, and cooperative target reconnaissance:

\[R_i(t) = R_{\text{step}} + R_{\text{target}, i}(t) - R_{\text{crash}, i}(t)\]

docs.title: 1.1 Component Breakdown
docs.text:
1. Step Survival Reward (\(R_{\text{step}} = +0.01\)): Awarded at every time step that the UAV remains airborne and operational. Encourages staying alive (prevents agents from learning to crash on purpose).

  2. Target Photography Reward (\(R_{\text{target}} = +1.0\)): Triggered when an uncollected target is successfully photographed within inspection radius \(D_{\text{photo}} = 45\text{ px}\) under stochastic camera uncertainty (\(X \sim \text{Bernoulli}(P_{\text{team}})\)):

    • Individual Reward Mode (team_reward = False, Default): $\(R_{\text{target}, i}(t) = \begin{cases} +1.0 & \text{if UAV } i \text{ was within } D_{\text{photo}} \text{ when photo succeeded} \\ 0.0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\)$

    • Shared Team Reward Mode (team_reward = True): The reward is split equally among all currently living swarm members:

      $\(R_{\text{target}, i}(t) = \frac{+1.0}{|\mathcal{V}_{\text{alive}}(t)|}\)$

  3. Crash Penalty (\(R_{\text{crash}} = -10.0\)): Assessed instantaneously when any vertex of UAV \(i\) penetrates an obstacle or boundary plane: $\(R_{\text{crash}, i}(t) = \begin{cases} -10.0 & \text{if UAV } i \text{ collides with boundary or obstacle} \\ 0.0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\)$

A collision causes an immediate crash (\(\text{alive}_i \leftarrow \text{False}\)).

docs.title: 2. Cumulative Return & Discount Factor
docs.text:
The reinforcement learning objective for each agent is to maximize its expected discounted return:

\[J_i(\pi) = \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{t=0}^T \gamma^t R_i(t) \right]\]

docs.title: 2.1 Discount Factor Selection
docs.text:
• Recommended Range: \(\gamma \in [0.95, 0.99]\) (default baseline: \(\gamma = 0.99\)).
  • Effective Planning Horizon: The effective horizon is given by \(H_{\text{eff}} = \frac{1}{1 - \gamma}\):
    • At \(\gamma = 0.95 \implies H_{\text{eff}} \approx 20\text{ steps}\) (\(\approx 0.67\text{ seconds}\) at \(30\text{ FPS}\)). Focuses narrowly on imminent obstacle avoidance.
    • At \(\gamma = 0.99 \implies H_{\text{eff}} \approx 100\text{ steps}\) (\(\approx 3.3\text{ seconds}\)). Enables drones to proactively position themselves vertically for upcoming targets while anticipating obstacles.

docs.title: 3. Episode Horizon: Termination vs. Truncation
docs.text: Following the standard Gymnasium / PettingZoo MDP specification, ScrollSwarm strictly distinguishes between terminations (natural environmental ends) and truncations (artificial time-limit bounds):

docs.title: 3.1 Terminations
docs.text:
• Evaluated on a per-agent basis.
  • An agent terminates (True) if and only if it collides with a boundary or an obstacle.
  • Once terminated, an agent is removed from env.agents for the remainder of the episode.
  • If all agents terminate, the multi-agent episode ends immediately.

docs.title: 3.2 Truncations
docs.text:
• Occurs when the global simulation step reaches the predefined horizon limit: $\(\text{step_count} \ge T_{\max} = 1000\text{ steps}\)$
  • When truncated, all remaining active agents receive truncations[agent_id] = True simultaneously.
  • Standard RL algorithms (e.g., PPO) use truncation to bootstrap the value function estimate \(V(s_{T_{\max}})\) without misinterpreting the cutoff as a failure.
